Understanding Jev-Style System One Models: Does Structure Reduce Selection Bias?
理解Jev风格系统一模型：结构是否降低选择偏差？
Selection bias in large language models (LLMs) can persist despite instructions to ignore presentation order or prompts that elicit reasoning. Recent efforts to reproduce Jev-style System One behavior have produced a growing family of models that predict probabilities directly over supplied candidates. Yet systematic comparisons of selection bias across Jev versions, Jev reproductions, and generative LLMs remain limited in multi-option tasks. This leaves a central question: does Jev-style decision structure reduce selection bias? We address this question with a simple test that shuffles options while keeping question and candidate content fixed. Across two Jev versions, twelve Jev reproductions, and six generative LLMs, we trace individual answers through eight presentations and compare them with fixed-order repetition. On our primary collection of 1,700 questions from two benchmarks, Jev's accuracy varies by less than two percentage points, yet its cumulative failure set expands by 27--29\% relative to the original order, with first failures continuing into the final presentation. This loss of initial successes is substantially larger than under fixed-order repetition, even for highly repeatable Jev reproductions. Nor does Jev show a general advantage over the LLM baselines in preserving correct choices. Aggregation offers limited protection: voting yields modest gains for Jev, while even unanimous answers are frequently wrong. These results expose a gap between repeatable decisions and decisions that remain correct across equivalent presentations, showing why stable accuracy alone cannot establish resistance to selection bias.
中文翻译
大型语言模型中的选择偏差即使在指示忽略呈现顺序或使用引发推理的提示时仍可能持续存在。近期重现Jev风格系统一行为的努力产生了越来越多的模型，这些模型直接对提供的候选项预测概率。然而，在多选项任务中，对不同Jev版本、Jev复现模型与生成式大语言模型的选择偏差进行系统比较仍然有限。这引出一个核心问题：Jev风格决策结构是否能降低选择偏差？我们通过一个简单测试来回答这一问题——在保持问题和候选内容不变的情况下打乱选项顺序。在两个Jev版本、十二个Jev复现模型和六个生成式大语言模型上，我们追踪了8次呈现下的个体答案，并与固定顺序重复进行对比。在包含1700个问题的主数据集上，Jev的准确率变化小于2个百分点，但其累积失败集相比原始顺序扩大了27%–29%，首次失败持续到最终呈现。这种初始成功损失远大于固定顺序重复的情况，即使对于高度可重复的Jev复现模型也是如此。此外，Jev在保持正确选择方面并未表现出对大语言模型基线的普遍优势。聚合方法提供有限保护：投票仅给Jev带来适度增益，而即使一致的答案也经常错误。这些结果揭示了可重复决策与在等价呈现下仍保持正确的决策之间的差距，说明仅靠稳定的准确率无法证明对选择偏差的抵抗力。

Quantifying Claim Smoothing by LLM Research Agents
量化大语言模型研究代理的主张平滑现象
Deep research, or any use of large language models (LLMs) to read a large document collection and produce insights, requires synthesizing information from different sources. In this work, we find that LLMs produce long-form research reports that read as confident syntheses but which fail to accurately reflect the underlying documents. We call this failure smoothing. In collapsing diverse and potentially conflicting sources into a single narrative, the model discards the evidential "jaggedness" of its corpus and asserts conclusions more decisive than the citations can support. We introduce a claim level scoring pipeline, SmoothScore, to quantify this effect. Our pipeline extracts key conclusive claims from model generated reports, then finds evidence relevant to each claim and clusters that evidence along high level aspects. Finally, each claim is scored with respect to the evidence to quantify the degree of smoothing done by the agent. Across 7 systems and 4 datasets, we find that agents consistently produce stronger claims than warranted.
中文翻译
深度研究，即利用大语言模型阅读大量文档集合并生成洞见，需要从不同来源综合信息。本研究发现，大语言模型生成的长篇研究报告读起来充满自信的综合，但实际上未能准确反映底层文档。我们将这种失败称为“平滑”。在将多样且可能冲突的来源整合为单一叙述的过程中，模型丢弃了其语料库中的证据“锯齿状”特征，并断言比引用所能支持的更为决断的结论。我们引入了一个主张级别的评分流程SmoothScore，用于量化这一效应。该流程从模型生成的报告中提取关键结论性主张，然后寻找与每个主张相关的证据，并按高层次维度对证据进行聚类。最后，根据证据对每个主张进行评分，以量化代理所造成的平滑程度。在7个系统和4个数据集上，我们发现代理始终产生强于实际支持的主张。

SEMA-Auto: Sighted and Efficient Multi-Turn Attack with Autonomy
SEMA-Auto：具备视觉感知与自主性的高效多轮攻击
Existing jailbreak attackers fall into two classes: static planners fix their single- or multi-turn adversarial plans in advance, remaining simple but losing sight of the victim's replies, wasting turns and limiting transferability; interactive generators read each victim reply to generate the next-turn attack but require in-loop evaluators for success signals or hints, incurring substantial costs and inflated performance. Bridging this gap, we propose SEMA-Auto, a sighted and efficient multi-turn attacker with autonomy, interacting with the victim model and terminating the session by itself upon success. To stabilize its behaviors and boost its capabilities, SEMA-Auto is trained in two stages. Synthetic bootstrap tuning installs the notion of attack targets and conforming decisions by fine-tuning the base model with bootstrapped trajectories. Decision-supervised reinforcement learning then optimizes two objectives jointly yet separately, reinforcing the attack with higher jailbreak reward while supervising the decision at each turn against an absolute target. Our method achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) attack success rates (ASR) across multiple datasets, victims, and judges, outperforming all static and interactive baselines, within almost the fewest turns, demonstrating both effectiveness and efficiency. For example, SEMA-Auto performs a $76.0\%$ ASR@1 within an average of $3.0$ turns against DeepSeek-V4-Flash on AdvBench, while the best static baseline is $54.8\%$ with fixed $7$ turns and the best interactive baseline is $43.8\%$ in $3.7$ turns. Against safety-hardened frontier models, GPT-oss-120B, GPT-5.4, Claude-Haiku-4.5, and GPT-6-Astra, our counter-trained attacker achieves an average $59.6\%$ ASR@1 on HarmBench, $13.8\%$ over prior SOTA. Our code is available at: https://github.com/microsoft/SEMA
中文翻译
现有的越狱攻击者分为两类：静态规划者预先固定单轮或多轮对抗计划，虽然简单但会忽视目标回复，浪费轮次并限制迁移能力；交互生成器则逐轮读取目标回复以生成下一轮攻击，但需要循环内评估器提供成功信号或提示，导致高昂成本和性能虚高。为弥合这一差距，我们提出SEMA-Auto，一种具备视觉感知与自主性的高效多轮攻击者，能够与目标模型交互并在成功时自行终止会话。为稳定其行为并增强能力，SEMA-Auto采用两阶段训练。合成自举调优通过用自举轨迹微调基础模型，植入攻击目标和合规决策的概念；决策监督强化学习则联合但独立优化两个目标：通过更高的越狱奖励强化攻击，同时在每一轮对决策施加绝对目标的监督。我们的方法在多个数据集、目标模型和评判者上均达到最先进的攻击成功率（ASR），优于所有静态和交互基线，且几乎在最少轮次内完成，展现出高效与有效。例如，SEMA-Auto在AdvBench上对DeepSeek-V4-Flash实现76.0%的ASR@1，平均仅需3.0轮，而最佳静态基线为54.8%（固定7轮），最佳交互基线为43.8%（3.7轮）。在经过安全加固的前沿模型GPT-oss-120B、GPT-5.4、Claude-Haiku-4.5和GPT-6-Astra上，我们的对抗训练攻击者在HarmBench上实现平均59.6%的ASR@1，比先前SOTA高出13.8%。代码已公开于：https://github.com/microsoft/SEMA

From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing
从自我信心到统计准确性：基于直接审计与LLM辅助审计的规模化人机评估
For large language models (LLMs) and multimodal large language models (MLLMs), model-reported self-confidence is often miscalibrated, yet it may still be useful for efficient evaluation. At the same time, LLM-as-a-judge offers a scalable alternative to direct human auditing, but its practical benefit depends on calibration quality and inference cost. This paper develops a unified statistical framework for both evaluation routes under alternative sampling strategies. For direct auditing, confidence-stratified sampling is used to recover population accuracy from partially verified outputs without requiring calibrated confidence. Finite-sample uncertainty is characterized, and the analysis shows how highly uneven confidence strata affect audit efficiency and label allocation. For judge-assisted evaluation, the judge is modeled through sensitivity and false-positive rate, yielding an error-corrected estimator with calibration uncertainty. The two routes are then compared through human-label and total-cost efficiency boundaries. Experiments on MMLU-Pro and MMMU-Pro show that miscalibrated self-confidence can still support statistically valid stratified auditing. Under highly imbalanced confidence distributions, proportional allocation substantially reduces estimation error relative to equal-per-stratum allocation. For judge-assisted evaluation, only a small subset of target--verifier pairs satisfies the idealized human-label efficiency condition, and automated inference costs can further limit potential savings. These findings clarify the statistical and economic conditions under which confidence-guided auditing and automated verification are useful.
中文翻译
对于大语言模型（LLMs）和多模态大语言模型（MLLMs），模型报告的自我信心常常存在校准偏差，但仍可能用于高效评估。同时，LLM作为评判者为直接人工审计提供了可扩展的替代方案，但其实际效益取决于校准质量与推理成本。本文构建了一个统一的统计框架，用于在不同采样策略下评估这两种路径。针对直接审计，采用信心分层采样，可在不依赖校准信心的情况下从部分验证输出中恢复总体准确率。分析了有限样本下的不确定性，并揭示了高度不均衡的信心层级如何影响审计效率与标签分配。对于评判者辅助评估，通过敏感性和假阳性率建模评判者，得到具有校准不确定性的误差修正估计器。随后通过人工标签效率和总成本效率边界对两种路径进行比较。在MMLU-Pro和MMMU-Pro上的实验表明，即使自我信心存在偏差，仍可支持统计上有效的分层审计。在信心分布高度不平衡时，按比例分配显著降低了相对于每层等量分配的估计误差。对于评判者辅助评估，仅有少数目标-验证者组合满足理想的人工标签效率条件，且自动化推理成本可能进一步限制潜在节省。这些发现明确了信心引导审计与自动化验证有用的统计与经济条件。

Evaluating DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks
评估DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017在失控与有害操控风险方面的表现
As frontier language models grow increasingly capable and autonomous, independent third-party evaluations are critical for characterizing their systemic safety risks. While closed-source releases are routinely accompanied by comprehensive system cards, open-weight models receive less scrutiny regarding frontier risks. To address this gap, we present an independent safety evaluation of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017, the latest version of V4.1 Flash that departs from V4 with a new architecture, scaled-up training, and strong agentic capabilities. Drawing on the EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice, we evaluate the model across 34 benchmarks, including 5 in-house suites, spanning evaluation integrity, loss of control, and harmful manipulation. Conforming to the AEF-1 standard, we compare V4.1 Flash-1017 against V4.1 Flash, earlier DeepSeek V4 models, and leading closed-source systems (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, and Gemini 3.8 Flash). Overall, V4.1 Flash-1017 shows substantial safety improvements over the V4 generation and approaches or matches leading closed-source baselines on several dimensions, while still exhibiting notable behaviors that warrant continued attention. Building on our findings, we highlight three key observations and recommendations. First, because safety can shift and even regress across minor updates, developers should integrate safety evaluation into incremental releases. Second, as final-turn outputs and end-state checks alone cannot reliably detect loss-of-control behaviors, deployments require process-level observability across both reasoning traces and action logs. Third, because public benchmarks elicit strong evaluation awareness and face data contamination risks, developing private benchmarks is essential for trustworthy frontier evaluation.
中文翻译
随着前沿语言模型的能力和自主性不断增强，独立第三方评估对于刻画其系统性安全风险至关重要。尽管闭源发布通常伴随全面的系统卡片，但开源权重模型在前沿风险方面的审查较少。为填补这一空白，我们对DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017——V4.1 Flash最新版本（相较于V4采用新架构、更大规模训练并具备强代理能力）进行了独立安全评估。依据欧盟通用人工智能行为准则，我们在34个基准测试上进行评估，涵盖5个内部套件，涉及评估完整性、失控风险和有害操控。符合AEF-1标准，我们将V4.1 Flash-1017与V4.1 Flash、早期DeepSeek V4模型以及领先闭源系统（GPT-6 Astra、GPT-5.6 Sol和Gemini 3.8 Flash）进行对比。总体而言，V4.1 Flash-1017相比V4代在安全性上有显著提升，并在多个维度上接近或达到领先闭源基线水平，但仍表现出一些值得持续关注的行为。基于研究发现，我们提出三点关键观察与建议：第一，由于安全性可能在微小更新中发生转移甚至退化，开发者应将安全评估纳入增量发布流程；第二，仅依靠最终输出和终态检查无法可靠检测失控行为，部署需具备跨推理轨迹与操作日志的过程可观测性；第三，由于公开基准易引发强烈评估意识并面临数据污染风险，开发私有基准对于可信的前沿评估至关重要。

Beyond Words Alone: Disentangling Distributed Evidence for Visually Grounded Cultural Translation
超越文字本身：解耦视觉基础文化翻译中的分布式证据
Social media enables cross-lingual communication, yet the meaning of user-generated content (UGC) is often distributed across text, images, and cultural knowledge, making translation challenging. Existing evaluations typically treat images as optional and assume textual information is sufficient, obscuring whether errors stem from missing visual evidence or inadequate cultural adaptation. We introduce \textbf{Culture-MMT}, a diagnostic benchmark for \textbf{distributed-evidence pragmatic reconstruction} in social-media translation. It contains 498 curated, de-identified UGC instances across 20 domains, categorized into Symbol, Visual, and Hybrid by their required evidence. We also develop a human-aligned domain-specific judge, Judger, and a controlled evaluation framework that systematically varies the evidence available to translators. Across 17 model configurations, real images improve performance by +0.280 on Visual and +0.197 on Hybrid, but only +0.050 on Symbol, while random images provide no comparable gains. Human-authored descriptions further show that jointly dependent cases remain more challenging even when visual facts are explicit. These results characterize culturally effective social-media translation as {meaning reconstruction from distributed evidence}, highlighting visual grounding and cultural-pragmatic adaptation as distinct model bottlenecks.
中文翻译
社交媒体促进了跨语言交流，但用户生成内容（UGC）的意义往往分布在文本、图像和文化知识中，使翻译变得困难。现有评估通常将图像视为可选因素，假设文本信息已足够，从而掩盖了错误究竟是源于缺失视觉证据还是文化适应不足。我们引入了 extbf{Culture-MMT}，一个针对社交媒体翻译中 extbf{分布式证据语用重构}的诊断基准。该基准包含498个精心筛选、去标识化的UGC实例，覆盖20个领域，按所需证据类型分为符号型、视觉型和混合型三类。我们还开发了一个与人类对齐的领域特定评判者Judger，以及一个可控评估框架，系统性地改变翻译者可用的证据。在17种模型配置下，真实图像在视觉型任务上提升+0.280，在混合型任务上提升+0.197，但在符号型任务上仅提升+0.050；随机图像则无类似增益。人工撰写的描述进一步表明，即使视觉事实明确，联合依赖情况依然更具挑战性。这些结果将文化有效社交翻译定义为{从分布式证据中重建意义}，凸显了视觉锚定与文化语用适应作为模型瓶颈的独立性。

MANTIS: Multi-Axis News Transformations for Instance-Wise Stress Testing and Worst-Case Training in Fake News Detection
MANTIS：多轴新闻转换用于实例级压力测试与最坏情况训练的假新闻检测
Automated fake news detection is vital on social media, where fake news is easily rewritten to fool detectors. However, existing approaches typically rely on superficial writing cues or single-style text rewrites, resulting in poor robustness under diverse cosmetic modifications. We construct MANTIS-Bench, a multi-axis presentation-attack benchmark that pairs original news with rewritten views across writing style, emotional expression, and dissemination framing. We further propose MANTIS, an instance-adaptive adversarial framework enabling dynamic worst-case training tailored to each news article with zero inference-time overhead. This reframes fake news defense from heuristic format smoothing into targeted, fact-invariant credibility assessment. Experiments on MANTIS-Bench show that MANTIS reduces the Union Attack Success Rate (UASR) by 3.55 percentage points relative to SheepDog on GossipCop and consistently outperforms prior single-axis defenses on Macro-F1 while maintaining competitive clean accuracy, demonstrating the effectiveness of multi-axis and instance-adaptive worst-case training.
中文翻译
自动化假新闻检测在社交媒体中至关重要，因为假新闻常被改写以欺骗检测器。然而，现有方法通常依赖表面写作线索或单一风格的文本重写，导致在多样化的外观修改下鲁棒性差。我们构建了MANTIS-Bench，一个包含多轴呈现攻击的基准，将原始新闻与在写作风格、情感表达和传播框架三个维度上重写的版本配对。我们进一步提出了MANTIS，一种实例自适应对抗框架，能够为每篇新闻文章动态生成最坏情况训练，且无需推理时开销。这将假新闻防御从启发式格式平滑转变为针对性、事实无关的可信度评估。在MANTIS-Bench上的实验表明，MANTIS相比SheepDog在GossipCop上将联合攻击成功率（UASR）降低了3.55个百分点，并在宏F1上持续优于先前单轴防御方法，同时保持了竞争力的干净准确率，证明了多轴与实例自适应最坏情况训练的有效性。

ImgMT: Wikipedia-based Dataset For Evaluating Text-in-Image Translation
ImgMT：基于维基百科的图像内文本翻译评估数据集
Text-in-image translation aims to translate all textual content embedded in an image. In Text Image Translation (TIT), the output is translated text; In-Image Machine Translation (IIMT) additionally renders the translation back into the image. We introduce ImgMT, a massively multilingual dataset and benchmark mined from localized SVG illustrations on Wikimedia Commons, focusing on diagrams, maps, and infographics. ImgMT contains 35,612 aligned image pairs grouped into 1,855 image sets, spanning 129 languages, 20+ writing systems, and 4,886 language pairs. We propose a multi-level evaluation protocol that measures source-side text-region detection and OCR accuracy alongside target-side translation quality. We benchmark several multimodal large language models and a dedicated TIT system in English->X and X->English settings, and find that the source language and writing system substantially affect TIT quality. Finally, we show that ImgMT is not well suited for isolating the contribution of visual information in multimodal translation.
中文翻译
图像内文本翻译旨在翻译嵌入在图像中的所有文本内容。在文本图像翻译（TIT）中，输出为翻译后的文本；而在图像内机器翻译（IIMT）中，还需将翻译结果重新渲染回图像。我们引入ImgMT，一个从维基媒体共用资源上的本地化SVG插图中挖掘出的海量多语言数据集与基准测试集，重点关注图表、地图和信息图。ImgMT包含35,612对对齐图像，分为1,855个图像组，覆盖129种语言、20多种书写系统以及4,886种语言对。我们提出一个多层级评估协议，衡量源端文本区域检测与OCR准确率，以及目标端翻译质量。我们在英语→X和X→英语设置下对多个多模态大语言模型和专用TIT系统进行了基准测试，发现源语言和书写系统显著影响TIT质量。最后，我们表明ImgMT并不适合隔离视觉信息在多模态翻译中的贡献。

MechAlign: Evaluating Semantic Alignment at the Project Level in Mathematical Formalization
MechAlign：在数学形式化项目层面评估语义对齐
Lean verifies that a formal proof establishes its stated proposition under declared assumptions, but does not check whether that proposition faithfully expresses the mathematical claim in a manuscript. Assessing this correspondence requires interpreting the main theorem through its project dependencies, which may be scattered throughout a large development. We introduce MechAlign, a framework for project-level semantic alignment review that combines formal dependency extraction with LLM-based assessment. Its extraction tool, LeanTrace, constructs a statement dependency graph from elaborated declarations, retaining definition bodies and structure constraints while excluding proof bodies and stopping at an explicit library boundary. The reviewer uses this context to investigate alignment and report discrepancies with localized evidence. We conduct a preliminary review of 201 main results from 173 OpenAI Math projects, using supplied informal descriptions and available paper context. The number of paper submissions to major AI conferences has increased dramatically in recent years, substantially increasing the peer-review workload of researchers. At the same time, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support peer review, both by individual reviewers and by conference organizations. While LLM capabilities have improved considerably, their evaluations may be influenced by linguistic characteristics that are unrelated to scientific content. In this work, we introduce a controlled experimental framework for studying such effects by systematically perturbing the linguistic style of research papers. Specifically, we rewrite papers to exhibit (i) linguistic features associated with native or non-native English writing, and (ii) high- or low-confidence linguistic features. To construct these interventions, we derive fine-grained rewriting instructions grounded in the linguistic literature and apply them using LLMs. Crucially, our interventions are designed to preserve the underlying scientific content. We then evaluate the resulting papers using different LLM reviewers. Our experiments expose a critical vulnerability in LLM-based peer review: reviewers systematically reward confident rhetoric independent of scientific content, raising serious concerns about the robustness of their assessments.

While prior work reports strong predictive performance, it remains unclear whether these systems produce reliable and robust text annotations. The value of language models for any community depends on whether a model actually understands the culture of the people it intends to serve. We use the Igbo language as a case study. Existing benchmarks test translated Western ideas, lacking depth. To address this, we introduce CAB-Igbo, a benchmark developed from indigenous cultural sources and verified by native speakers across six domains. We evaluated diverse models under varying conditions, incorporating regional personas. Performance was assessed using multiple-choice accuracy and human evaluations across Epistemic Fidelity, Representational Richness, Linguistic Quality, and Pragmatic Proficiency. Results reveal a stark dissociation between language fluency and cultural knowledge. Through statistical testing, we show that for most models, the severe lack of Epistemic Fidelity and Representational Richness is already present in English and does not significantly worsen when switching to Igbo. Instead, native language prompting mainly degrades Linguistic Quality and Pragmatic Proficiency. Gemini 2.0 Flash is the only model whose cultural knowledge scores improve under Igbo prompting. We find that current models struggle to demonstrate the knowledge needed for true alignment with Igbo, and multiple-choice formats allow pattern-matching to appear as understanding. Furthermore, automated judges agree with humans on linguistic quality but fail on epistemic fidelity. Ultimately, cultural evaluation must be built from community knowledge, establishing human evaluation as the gold standard to prevent misrepresenting low-resource communities globally.

Alignment sKL, the divergence between von Mises-Fisher distributions fitted to synthetic and human-annotated queries, is an unlabelled proxy for parser F1 ($ρ=-0.917$ against human queries written for simulated shopper scenarios, lower is closer). Agent Skills allow LLM agents to combine reusable capabilities, but checking each Skill in isolation cannot rule out policy violations when they are composed. We term such failures Conflict of Skills (CoS): artifacts or assessment signals produced for one purpose may be reused downstream without preserving the restrictions or authorization needed for their new use. Using controlled executions of publicly available Skills and matched single-Skill controls, we identify four recurring mechanisms behind CoS. Building on these findings, we introduce the Conflict of Skills Attack (CoSA), which adds locally admitted Skills to an existing pool to supply missing business operations (capability supplementation) or reshape artifact exchange, decision reuse, and target/action bindings (relationship reshaping). CoSA leaves existing Skills and runtime permissions unchanged. To evaluate this threat under autonomous Skill selection, we introduce CoSA-Bench, built from real-world Skills and controlled services, with 288 tasks across recruiting, finance, IT, and business, covering data leakage, unauthorized state modification, and unsafe execution. Across five LLMs and three agent harnesses, additions capped at 5% of each original pool raise the policy-violation rate from 35.02% to 58.45%, an increase of 23.43 percentage points. Trace analysis links compliant-to-violating transitions to cross-Skill dependencies involving the additions. Finally, we develop a lightweight harness-level guard that checks information flow and authorization before consequential actions. On OpenClaw recruiting tasks across five models, the guard reduces violations from 65.28% to 6.67%, while policy-compliant task completion on matched benign controls changes from 66.67% to 65.00%.

GLP-1 medications are increasingly used for weight management, and many people share their experiences online. These narratives show why people take the drugs and what they experience, but they remain unstructured and disconnected from formal pharmacovigilance. We therefore present AskGLP1, a system that transforms online patient narratives into a knowledge graph (KG) and answers questions about medication experiences. Through an LLM-assisted pipeline grounded in the MedDRA terminology, AskGLP1 screens nearly 8.5 million Reddit posts for medication experiences and distills 163,135 of them, with 2,506 WebMD reviews, into a KG of 385,790 drug-side-effect and drug-purpose relations. We find that GLP-1 experiences are source- and drug-specific. Online narratives share the most common gastrointestinal symptoms with FAERS, but they foreground everyday burdens such as fatigue and food aversion, whereas FAERS reports more often include injection-site reactions and selected serious diagnoses such as pancreatitis. We further find that posts report less nausea and vomiting for tirzepatide than for semaglutide, more fatigue for Wegovy than Ozempic and for Zepbound than Mounjaro. Evaluations show that the agent answers with verifiable evidence and declines requests for medical advice. Our findings reveal gaps between what FAERS captures and what people report online, and they call for patient-centered approaches to pharmacovigilance. Code, prompts, and evaluation questions are available at https://github.com/ZhaoqianXue/AskGLP1.

A numerical claim generated by a financial analyst agent can match a number in a company filing but refer to the wrong entity, concept, period, unit or scope. A check based on reference answers can mark such an answer as wrong but does not explain why it fails. In this paper, we present NumTrace, a new benchmark that audits the provenance of each numerical claim made by financial analyst agents: its source and financial semantics. NumTrace currently has 540 questions over 2,163 SEC EDGAR documents. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first numerical benchmark about who holds a company's shares (Form 13F) and what its executives are owed (Item 402(i)). On a frozen snapshot of these documents, we build the reference answers according to accounting rules. NumTrace then gives each claim three separate verdicts: value, binding and support. By retaining separate value and binding verdicts, NumTrace detects right number, wrong account (RNWA) errors: a claim has an RNWA error when it passes the value check but fails the binding check. The RNWA rate quantifies the gap between value-only and joint value-and-binding pass rates. Finally, we audit three agents, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. RNWA errors make up 67.5-81.8% of each agent's failing claims. In particular, on 13F co-filing group questions, about 91% of claims pass the value check, but fewer than half pass the binding check.

(arXiv:2509.01328) under a drastically smaller budget: models of at most 2B parameters, one 16 GB consumer GPU, about five GPU-days. (1) With matched data and labels, text is the bottleneck: on the same 100k-decision training set, a 2.6M-parameter convolutional board encoder agrees with the strong AI Mortal on 80.6% of test decisions, above every text-prompt LLM we train (best 77.8%), and places better at the table (2.85 over 1,000 games vs. ~3.0 for the LLMs; paired difference at n=100 not significant). (3) Few-point agreement differences do not resolve into playing strength within a family: +2.5 agreement points coincide with a paired placement difference of +0.02 +/- 0.12 ranks (p=1.0), and +2.0 points at 2B with -0.06 (p=0.37) - both below the ~0.25-rank resolution of 100 paired games. We also document a paper-code mismatch in the original winner filter, reconstruct its two private engine patches, and show that a divide-and-conquer pipeline makes template-generated Japanese rationales 93% sentence-exact (43% without facts). Per Tenhou's terms we release no trained weights - only code, configurations, and evaluation protocols.

User memory helps personalized systems build on their understanding of users over time. In e-commerce, users convey their preferences and needs through both explicit language and implicit interactions with products. We study memory built from logs of these interactions, examining how it can \emph{remember} concrete evidence and established interests, and use that evidence to \emph{infer} underlying needs and preferences that inform judgments beyond well-observed product domains. Existing memory methods primarily target language-based interactions, and evaluations offer limited real behavioral data and limited separation of these capabilities. This leaves open how to jointly support and separately evaluate remembering and inference from behavioral logs. We formulate the problem of continual behavioral user memory around these joint requirements and develop a dedicated evaluation framework and memory method to address them. \textbf{BehaviorMemBench} is a benchmark built from real e-commerce logs covering 1{,}194 users and 17{,}462 behavioral batches over more than three years, with automatic future-behavior labels and a task-independent memory interface to separately evaluate remembering and inference under a common protocol. \textbf{BehaviorMem} is a memory design that organizes explicit behavioral facts and inferred user characteristics across long-term and short-term scopes in a two-axis state, with evidence-grounded formation, continual maintenance, and query-independent readout. Experiments across two builders and two task readers show that BehaviorMem leads the evaluated agentic memories on remember and infer, and reveal different method rankings across the two capabilities and competitive statistical baselines. Validation on a public dataset further supports its usefulness for downstream tasks based on behavioral histories.

From Belief Inference to Task Action: A Multi-Level Evaluation of Theory of Mind on Verifiable Tasks

Effective collaboration requires language models to understand what others know and believe, and to act accordingly. Models that assume others share their information may omit necessary communication and undermine coordination. Many theory-of-mind (ToM) benchmarks assess mental-state inference through story questions, but correct answers do not establish that models can use these judgments in subsequent tasks. We introduce a multi-level evaluation built on existing, verifiable tasks. We extend household collaboration and calendar scheduling with asymmetric information while retaining their original constraints and validators. Independent interfaces assess world understanding, information access, beliefs, decisions, and execution. Controls supply personal evidence or correct beliefs to distinguish state recovery from state use. Across six model configurations, these abilities diverge. On matched scheduling cases, Claude recovers all agent beliefs correctly but produces subjectively optimal plans in only 67.9% of cases. In household collaboration, supplying beliefs raises Qwen-27B success from 55.0% to 75.0%, yet Qwen-4B answers every fixed supplied-belief source question correctly while completing only 20.0% of the corresponding continuation condition. These results show why ToM evaluation must connect perspective inference to independently verified decisions and task consequences.

有效协作要求语言模型理解他人的认知状态与信念，并据此采取行动。若模型假设他人共享自身信息，则可能遗漏必要沟通，破坏协调。许多心智理论（ToM）基准通过故事问答评估心理状态推断，但正确答案并不能证明模型能将这些判断用于后续任务。我们引入基于现有可验证任务的多层级评估体系。我们在家庭协作与日程安排任务中引入不对称信息，同时保留原有约束与验证机制。独立接口分别评估世界理解、信息获取、信念状态、决策与执行。控制条件提供个人证据或正确信念，以区分状态恢复与状态使用。在六种模型配置中，这些能力表现出明显分化。在匹配的日程安排案例中，Claude能正确恢复所有代理信念，但仅在67.9%情况下生成主观最优计划。在家庭协作任务中，提供信念使Qwen-27B成功率从55.0%提升至75.0%，而Qwen-4B虽能正确回答所有给定信念来源的问题，却仅完成20.0%的相应延续任务。这些结果表明，ToM评估必须将视角推理与独立验证的决策及任务后果相连接。

In high-stakes domains such as finance, critical information evolves through multi-party interaction. Recovering these changes and their sources is fundamental to reliable speech understanding. Existing speech benchmarks focus on transcription, local understanding, and turn-level state prediction, leaving joint decision evolution across speakers insufficiently evaluated. We introduce DecisionTraceBench, a speech state-tracking benchmark for Decision-Critical Information State Tracking (DCIST). It jointly evaluates decision event sequences, speaker attribution, scope, and temporal evidence, using trajectory-level F1 to measure complete event-chain recovery. Our dataset comprises Chinese financial dialogues involving two to four speakers, with 100.39 hours of synthetic audio and 8.61 hours of human-performed recordings. On a fixed cohort of human-performed recordings, five cascaded systems and two direct-audio models achieve DCIST scores of 5.73% to 21.35%. Ablations with speaker-labeled reference scripts and no temporal localization requirements yield a maximum score of only 38.72%. Audio perturbation experiments further show that overall transcription error rates do not adequately reflect complete trajectory recovery. These findings reveal limitations in jointly understanding information provenance and state evolution, providing a benchmark for evaluating decision-process understanding and decision traceability in high-stakes speech applications.

在金融等高风险领域，关键信息通过多方互动不断演变。恢复这些变化及其来源是实现可靠语音理解的基础。现有的语音基准主要关注转录、局部理解及回合级状态预测，未能充分评估跨说话人联合决策的演化过程。我们提出了DecisionTraceBench，一个用于决策关键信息状态追踪（DCIST）的语音状态追踪基准。该基准联合评估决策事件序列、说话人归属、作用范围和时间证据，并使用轨迹级F1分数衡量完整事件链的恢复情况。我们的数据集包含涉及两到四名说话人的中文金融对话，包含100.39小时合成音频和8.61小时真人录音。在固定的人类录音样本上，五个级联系统和两个直接音频模型的DCIST得分在5.73%至21.35%之间。通过使用带说话人标注的参考脚本并取消时间定位要求的消融实验，最高得分仅为38.72%。音频扰动实验进一步表明，整体转录错误率并不能充分反映完整轨迹的恢复情况。这些发现揭示了在联合理解信息来源与状态演化方面的局限性，为评估高风险语音应用中的决策过程理解和决策可追溯性提供了基准。

LADDER: Diagnosing Domain-Level Self-Assessment Under Noisy Feedback
LADDER：在噪声反馈下诊断领域级自我评估
Knowing when they are reliable is essential for language models to support human-AI collaboration. Yet interaction feedback is not always complete or correct, and may mislead models' understanding of their own capabilities. We introduce LADDER to study how language models assess themselves under unreliable feedback. Our findings show that models can accurately report supplied performance information while still struggling to form trustworthy self-assessments from interaction experience. Apparently accurate assessments can obscure capability differences and do not necessarily predict future task performance. These findings suggest that trustworthy self-assessment should be evaluated against observed task performance and its predictive value. Our study provides empirical evidence of the limits of model self-knowledge and a basis for evaluating capability awareness in reliable human-AI collaboration.

iPrefBench: A User-Centric Benchmark for Personalized Mobile Use Agents
iPrefBench：面向个性化移动使用代理的用户中心基准
An agent that truly knows and acts on behalf of its user has been a long-standing promise of AI assistants. Computer-use agents bring this promise within reach by capably executing fully specified tasks across apps. However, real-world user requests are often underspecified. To act correctly for the particular user, an agent must infer some missing information from the user's activity history and ask for other information that only the user can provide, without making unsupported assumptions or burdening the user with unnecessary questions. We present iPrefBench, a benchmark for evaluating the infer and ask capabilities of personal mobile-use agents in an executable iOS environment with an interactive simulated user. Grounded in a coherent persona with 3,051 past activity events, iPrefBench comprises 130 underspecified user tasks across 26 apps. Each omitted user-dependent requirement is, by construction, either history-inferable or ask-only. iPrefBench evaluates personalized mobile agents on both whether agents complete tasks correctly for the user (i.e., personalized task completion) and whether they seek user input when necessary (i.e., user-agent interaction). Evaluation of 7 frontier agents reveals a substantial gap between execution and personalization. Agents achieve high action completion scores (up to 91.6%) but low full task success (up to 47.7%) because personalization lags behind. They especially struggle with ask-only information, failing to request enough necessary information. Our findings highlight a challenge for personalized agents in knowing what to infer and when to ask. We hope that iPrefBench can serve as a valuable testbed for building agents that know their user and work with them.

真正了解并代表用户行动的智能体一直是AI助手的长期承诺。计算机使用代理通过在多个应用中成功执行完全指定的任务，使这一承诺成为现实。然而，现实世界中的用户请求往往不完整。为了正确服务于特定用户，代理必须从用户的活动历史中推断部分缺失信息，并向用户询问只有用户才能提供的信息，同时避免做出未经证实的假设或给用户带来不必要的提问负担。我们提出了iPrefBench，一个在可执行iOS环境中通过交互式模拟用户评估个性化移动使用代理的推理与询问能力的基准。该基准基于一个包含3,051个过去活动事件的一致人格设定，涵盖26个应用中的130个不完整用户任务。每个被省略的用户相关需求，按构造原则，要么可通过历史推断，要么只能通过询问获得。iPrefBench评估个性化移动代理在是否能正确完成用户任务（即个性化任务完成率）以及是否在必要时主动寻求用户输入（即用户-代理交互）两方面的表现。对前沿代理的评估显示，执行与个性化之间存在显著差距。代理在动作完成率上表现良好（最高达91.6%），但全任务成功率较低（最高仅47.7%），因为个性化能力滞后。尤其在仅需询问的信息上表现不佳，未能提出足够必要的问题。研究结果突显了个性化代理在判断何时推断、何时询问方面的挑战。我们希望iPrefBench能成为构建真正了解用户并与之协作的智能体的重要测试平台。

Latency-sensitive spoken agents must know not only which tool to call, but also when they have heard enough to act. Waiting for the turn to complete delays execution even when the request is already actionable. However, neither existing spoken agents nor spoken dialogue corpora define the earliest point at which a request becomes actionable. We introduce a synthetic spoken-dialogue pipeline that provides earliest-actionable-point supervision, marking when the observed speech grounds a tool and its required arguments. Through controlled task generation, speech synthesis and alignment, and gated annotation, we construct 26,694 dialogues totaling 786 hours across 48 domains, with disjoint training and test argument values. We additionally create an audio rendering of $τ^2$-bench for external evaluation. We train an omni-modal language model on this corpus, enabling causal, chunk-level decisions and partial-transcript generation for downstream call completion. The model achieves tool-state macro-F1 scores of 0.48 and 0.47 on held-out dialogues and the external benchmark, respectively. For correct calls, the estimated mean lead over a turn-end cascade, using the same formatter, is 1.8-2.0 seconds in-domain and 1.1 seconds on $τ^2$-bench. These results demonstrate a data-driven path toward spoken agents that act while listening. We will open-source the pipeline and the training scripts.

对延迟敏感的口语代理不仅需要知道调用哪个工具，还需判断何时已听到足够信息以采取行动。等待发言结束再执行会延迟响应，即使请求已具备可执行条件。然而，现有口语代理和口语对话语料库均未定义请求变得可执行的最早时间点。我们提出一种合成口语对话流水线，提供最早可执行点的监督信号，标记观察到的语音何时足以支撑工具调用及其所需参数。通过受控任务生成、语音合成与对齐，以及门控标注，我们构建了总计786小时、覆盖48个领域的26,694条对话，训练与测试参数值互不重叠。我们还创建了$τ^2$-bench的音频版本用于外部评估。我们在该语料库上训练了一个全模态语言模型，支持因果性、分块级决策和下游调用完成的片段式文本生成。该模型在保留对话和外部基准上的工具状态宏F1得分分别为0.48和0.47。对于正确调用，使用相同格式化器估算出的平均领先时间在域内为1.8-2.0秒，在$τ^2$-bench上为1.1秒。这些结果展示了在语音代理边听边行动方面的数据驱动路径。我们将开源该流水线和训练脚本。

Entity Matching using Decision Models

Entity matching is the task of deciding whether two records describe the same real-world entity. Current entity matching methods rely on pre-trained language models (PLMs) which require task specific fine-tuning or generative large language models (LLMs) which do not require task-specific fine-tuning but are slow and expensive at matching large record sets. Decision models are a new class of LLM-based models that return a probability for each predefined answer option rather than generate text. This paper investigates decision models as an alternative to generative LLMs and fine-tuned PLMs for entity matching. We evaluate six decision models in a zero-shot setting across eight benchmarks and compare their performance with that of the generative LLM GPT-6 Luna and the PLM-based matcher Ditto. Our experiments show that, without task-specific training data, the four strongest decision models achieve mean F1 scores close to that of GPT-6 Luna, with the best model slightly surpassing it. This model also outperforms Ditto on six of the eight benchmarks. All decision models are faster than GPT-6 Luna, and most are less expensive. For three of the four strongest decision models, the predicted match probabilities are well calibrated without requiring any task-specific recalibration. A model cascade that routes the least confident record pairs to an ensemble of generative LLMs improves the mean F1 scores of the four strongest decision models by 1.9-4.0 percentage points. Using the best decision model and its best-performing prompt for each benchmark, the cascade surpasses the highest published F1 scores from literature on four of the eight benchmarks.

Large Language Models(LLMs) have shown strong performance on tasks with verifiable answers, but many real-world queries involve subjectivity, disagreement, and conflicting evidence. Most existing benchmarks for such queries remain English-centric, overlooking the vast diversity of perspectives held by users worldwide. To systematically study how LLM perspectives vary across languages, we curate PerspectivesQA, a manually verified multilingual dataset of globally contested topics covering 18 languages, and propose ROOTS, a framework that profiles linguistic, perspective, and framing diversity. We evaluate a diverse set of eight models covering both open-source and proprietary families at varying scales, establishing that LLMs hedge their answers in English but commit to positions in lower-resource languages. Larger models maintain a more consistent cross-lingual worldview, while smaller models are more easily swayed. All models also exhibit high sensitivity to minor surface-level input variations, producing notable stance even in larger models.

$Δτ$-Bench: Pushing Agents Toward a Moving Capability
Δτ-Bench：推动智能体应对动态能力挑战
In this paper, we introduce $Δτ$-Bench, an executable agent benchmark that models the structural evolution of large tool ecosystems. In $Δτ$-Bench, independently evolving services continually reshape how tasks can be accomplished: familiar tools may disappear or be replaced, while more efficient alternatives emerge amid overlapping functionality and noisy documentation. Against this moving capability frontier, we evaluate whether agents can proactively discover efficient tool-use paths and promptly revise their accumulated procedural knowledge, bringing together demands that existing benchmarks fail to examine. $Δτ$-Bench comprises 1,588 validated multi-turn tasks across 42 domains and six successive ecosystem states generated through capability-preserving transformations. Our evaluation shows that even the strongest evaluated model or harness achieves only 42.3% task success, while initial gains from existing skill-learning methods can not consistently translate into better adaptation as the ecosystem evolves. These findings motivate Steward, an ecosystem manager that jointly manages tools and procedural knowledge through incremental skill maintenance and dynamic provisioning during task execution. Experiments show that Steward sustains higher task success across ecosystem changes with lower skill-maintenance overhead, while improving both recovery from disrupted workflows and adoption of more efficient alternatives.

The LALA Benchmark: Evaluating Literary and Linguistic Analysis in LLMs

We introduce the Literature and Linguistics Analysis Benchmark (LALA), comprising 236 open-ended questions written by experts in linguistics and literary studies, together with expert-provided ideal answers. By comparing models within families and at similar training scales using human and LLM judges, LALA identifies differences in linguistic competence associated with post-training, offering a framework for evaluating future models and guiding targeted improvements. We administered questions to 17 language models and evaluated their responses using both human expert assessment and two LLM evaluators, Sol and Qwen. Base models displayed little of the linguistic competence assessed by the benchmark, whereas their post-trained versions performed markedly better, suggesting that post-training plays a central role in making linguistic knowledge accessible and usable. Parameter count, by contrast, showed no statistically significant association with partial-credit performance, and competencies remained unevenly distributed across linguistic domains. We interpret this pattern as evidence that post-training adds linguistic competencies piecemeal, without producing a general linguistic intelligence capable of extending them beyond the learned policies that support them. Models performed best on logical relations between statements and selected discourse-level tasks, while even the strongest post-trained models continued to struggle with ambiguity, literary style, reference, and misleading assumptions. Human and Sol evaluations produced nearly identical model rankings in both the original and ReliableEval runs, supporting the replicability of the comparative results.

Identically Trained Language Models Break on Different Jailbreaks
相同训练的语言模型在不同越狱攻击下表现各异
Jailbreak benchmarks test one checkpoint and treat which jailbreaks break it as a property of its pretraining data and safety training. We ask whether another pretraining run of the same data, given the same safety training, would break on the same jailbreaks. For each of 25 pretraining data recipes, we take 1B base models from 3 pretraining seeds and give each the same safety post-training with 2 post-training seeds, for 150 models in all. We then collect 20 responses from every model to a shared set of jailbreak prompts and correlate the per-prompt non-refusal rates between every pair of models. On average, two post-trained copies of the same pretraining run have per-prompt non-refusal rates that correlate at 0.984. A different pretraining seed lowers the correlation to 0.811, and a different data recipe lowers it only slightly further, to 0.779. These results indicate that which jailbreaks break a checkpoint depends much more on its pretraining run than on its data, a pattern that holds in all 25 data recipes and at 150M and 300M parameters. In practice, the best of 91 attack templates found on one checkpoint stays the best after a new pretraining seed in only 27% of model pairs, against 67% after a new post-training seed. Each pretraining run also leaves a fingerprint: across 3,211 prompts, a model's per-prompt non-refusal rates identify its pretraining run among all 75 runs every time, and a random subset of 50 prompts still does so 98% of the time.

LLMs are increasingly being used by users from diverse demographics with pluralistic values and distinct backgrounds. Maintaining safety while respecting value-laden personas is uniquely challenging because persona-conditioned requests are often not overtly malicious, unlike those in existing safety benchmarks. Alignment methods aimed at adversarial requests therefore may miss the harm that emerges from persona use, leaving models to either refuse legitimate value expression or blindly follow unsafe personas. We construct a dataset of 11k controversial topics paired with value-based personas mapping to value dimensions from the Schwartz Value Survey. Through an agentic pipeline that iteratively refines the topic and persona, we surface and collect harmful responses from well-aligned commercial LLMs with a more than 47% success rate. We use UNESCO's global citizenship principles as a minimal common ground for distinguishing valid value expressions from harmful behaviors, and introduce a controllable alignment model that lets users balance persona adherence and safety at inference time. The resulting model is safer and more persona-adherent than baselines on most samples.

On the encoder, the gap closes once both rates are chosen by the same search. StateWise: Teaching Language Models to Track and Obey Evolving Constraints in Multi-Turn Dialogue
StateWise：教导语言模型追踪并遵守多轮对话中的演化约束
Users of conversational assistants rarely state all requirements up front: they add constraints, amend them, withdraw them, digress, and return. Instruction-tuned LLMs fail here in two ways: active constraints stop being honored as turns accumulate (persistence failure), and withdrawn constraints keep being enacted (relapse). The only existing repair we know of is an external ledger that re-injects a compiled specification every turn. We propose StateWise, a self-improving approach that teaches a single LLM to maintain its own revisable constraint state, a typed state with tombstones for revoked constraints, so persistence and relapse are measured by executable checkers and ground-truth states are compiled for free. StateWise fine-tunes the LLM on two complementary skills, summarizing a dialogue into its constraint state and responding conditioned on that state, then self-trains on its own trajectories, keeping only turns that pass an exact round-trip check against the compiled state. This teaches 7-8B models to track the state almost perfectly but, surprisingly, not to obey it: on Llama-3.1-8B every supervised variant roughly doubles relapse. We therefore add a preference stage on self-generated relapse contrasts, where the rejected response enacts a revoked rule and the chosen one passes the round-trip check. On two backbones with held-out constraint families and unseen phrasings, StateWise cuts relapse by 8-22 points relative to supervised self-training, lifts conversation success by 8-19 points over the backbone, and beats an oracle compiled-ledger baseline on relapse with no inference-time scaffolding. We also characterize the recipe's cost on general instruction-following benchmarks and study weight interpolation as a mitigation.

对话助手的用户很少一次性说明所有需求：他们会添加约束、修改、撤回、偏离话题并返回。指令微调的大语言模型在此类场景中存在两种失败：随着对话轮次增加，活跃约束不再被遵守（持久性失败），而撤回的约束仍被继续执行（复发）。目前已知的唯一修复方法是外部账本，每轮重新注入编译后的规范。我们提出StateWise，一种自提升方法，教导单一语言模型维护可修订的约束状态——一种带有墓碑标记的类型化状态，以可执行检查器衡量持久性和复发性，且无需额外开销即可免费编译真实状态。StateWise在两个互补技能上对LLM进行微调：将对话总结为约束状态，以及基于该状态作出响应；随后在自身轨迹上进行自训练，仅保留与编译状态完全一致的回合。这使得7–8B模型几乎完美地追踪状态，但令人意外的是，却未能遵守它：在Llama-3.1-8B上，每个监督变体的复发率几乎翻倍。因此，我们引入偏好阶段，对自生成的复发对比进行训练，其中被拒绝的响应执行已被撤销的规则，而被选择的响应通过往返检查。在两个主干模型上，针对保留的约束族和未见表达方式，StateWise相比监督自训练将复发率降低8–22分，对话成功率提升8–19分，且在复发方面优于采用编译账本的基线，且无需推理时辅助结构。我们还分析了该方法在通用指令遵循基准上的代价，并研究权重插值作为缓解手段。

Can AI agents autonomously train useful language models and improve them using feedback from users? We introduce RSI Arena, a two-stage study of autonomous post-training as a step toward recursive self-improvement. Ten frontier models act as training agents, each starting from NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base. During a six-day first stage, each agent has 1,000 GPU-hours and $300 in API credit on a shared 64-GPU cluster, independently selecting data, implementing training procedures, and choosing checkpoints. We evaluate their models on 20 benchmarks and through blind human evaluations. All ten agents produce working assistants, with the strongest model, trained by GPT-6 Astra, closing a median of 76% of the base-to-Instruct gap across 12 capability benchmarks. Its human-preference rating is also close to NVIDIA Instruct after statistical adjustment for answer length and formatting. In Stage 2, each agent receives the comparison records and votes involving its Stage 1 model and is given three additional days for further training. Using NVIDIA Instruct as a common reference across the two evaluation rounds, we observe an improvement from Stage 1 to Stage 2 in the style-adjusted relative rating of eight of the ten models. We show that benchmark gains were modest, with no clear link to preference gains, while some agents encouraged longer responses and one model showed increased harmful compliance on StrongREJECT. RSI Arena provides an auditable setting for studying how human feedback can guide autonomous model development. It takes a step toward recursive self-improvement with human feedback (RSIHF), in which people help define what improvement means for the AI systems they use.

Mycelium: A Meta-Study of Hallucination Detection Across Provenance, Typology, and Granularities
Mycelium：跨来源、类型与粒度的幻觉检测元研究
Hallucination detection is increasingly important for evaluating and deploying large language models. However, existing methods are often compared across benchmarks that define and measure hallucination in substantially different ways, making reported scores difficult to interpret across settings. We study hallucination detection as a benchmark-conditioned measurement problem and organize existing benchmarks along three axes: provenance, which describes how model outputs and evidence conditions are obtained; typology, which captures the factuality and faithfulness failures represented by benchmark labels; and granularity, which specifies the unit at which hallucinations are annotated, predicted, and evaluated. Using this framework, we analyze how benchmark construction, annotation, and evaluation choices shape the underlying prediction task, and relate detector mechanisms and assumptions to the settings in which their performance is measured. We also examine span-level evaluation, where variation in annotation boundaries can substantially affect reported results, and propose Span Coverage F1 as a complementary containment-based metric. Our analysis clarifies what detector scores capture, highlights limitations of cross-benchmark comparisons, and motivates more explicit evaluation of generalization across benchmark conditions.

When the Weakest Language Keeps Moving: ARMOR-DP for Multilingual BabyLM
当最弱的语言持续移动时：面向多语言BabyLM的ARMOR-DP
Multilingual BabyLM systems usually fix language sampling proportions even though the weakest language can change during training. We present ARMOR-DP, a modular framework that diagnoses imbalance arising from representation, exposure, capacity, and objective pressure, and uses per-language validation loss to update sampling. Controlled experiments show that equal character budgets create a severe representation artifact for Chinese; byte-level encoding removes much of it, while static Chinese protection can subsequently make English the weakest language. The dynamic controller tracks these transitions and achieves a better score--balance tradeoff than fixed protection. On official evaluation, curriculum-dynamic checkpoints outperform a matched static Chinese-protective baseline while using fewer Chinese epochs; scaling capacity yields the strongest internal ARMOR-DP system. These results support a simple conclusion: multilingual weakness is a training-time state rather than a fixed property of a language. ARMOR-DP therefore separates diagnosis from intervention, allowing protection to follow the current bottleneck instead of a predetermined language label.

Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
Trajectory2Gym：面向工具使用智能体的决策基础组合式交互合成
Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. Even successful interactions may underrepresent multi-step dependencies or contain actions that are unjustified by the information visible to the agent at decision time. We identify two coupled requirements for effective trajectory supervision: compositional coverage, so that important observation-action dependencies are represented, and decision grounding, so that each supervised action is supported by the learner-visible interaction history. We introduce Trajectory2Gym, which constructs executable interactions around under-supported compositional structures and derives supervision only from grounded decisions in their realized executions. Structural-support selection allocates the resulting experience, while parent-normalized supervised fine-tuning preserves the semantic interaction as the unit of training weight. This reframes trajectory generation as the deliberate construction of learnable interaction experience, rather than the collection of successful trajectories. Across five Qwen3 scales, Trajectory2Gym improves Tau1, Tau2, and BFCL at every tested scale, increasing the equal-weight three-benchmark mean by 16.9-29.8 percentage points. The gains are strongest in stateful and multi-turn interaction, where later decisions depend on earlier observations and feedback. Our results suggest that scaling tool-use agents depends not only on collecting more successful trajectories, but on constructing interactions whose dependencies are represented and whose decisions are learnable from the agent's visible history.

成功的工具使用轨迹并不一定构成有效监督。即使成功交互也可能未能充分体现多步依赖关系，或包含在决策时刻不可见信息下无法合理解释的动作。我们识别出有效轨迹监督的两个耦合需求：组合覆盖性，确保重要的观察-动作依赖关系得到体现；决策根基性，确保每个受监督动作均得到学习者可见交互历史的支持。我们引入Trajectory2Gym，围绕支持不足的组合结构构造可执行交互，并仅从其实现执行中的根基性决策中提取监督信号。结构支持选择分配所得经验，父归一化监督微调则保持语义交互作为训练权重的基本单元。这将轨迹生成重新定义为有意识地构建可学习交互经验的过程，而非简单收集成功轨迹。在五个Qwen3规模上，Trajectory2Gym在所有测试规模下均提升了Tau1、Tau2和BFCL，使三个基准的等权重平均提升16.9至29.8个百分点。增益在有状态和多轮交互中最为显著，其中后续决策依赖于早期观察与反馈。我们的结果表明，提升工具使用智能体的能力不仅依赖于收集更多成功轨迹，更关键的是构建那些依赖关系得以体现且决策可从智能体可见历史中学习的交互。

SEDATE: Do Large Language Models Share an Aggression Circuit Across Languages?
SEDATE：大语言模型在跨语言中是否共享攻击性电路？
As the applications of AI continue to expand across various multimodal and multilingual domains, ensuring safe and responsible deployment of these systems has become an important concern. A wide-range of interventions have been proposed to make AI responses safer and more reliable. They often incur substantial computational or annotation costs, or cannot be extended to multilingual settings. In this work, we propose Selective Detection And Targeted Editing (SEDATE), a training-free approach based on detect-edit-verify strategy. SEDATE first detects the responsible neurons, edits them as and when necessary and finally verifies the model responses; all without any additional model training. We evaluate SEDATE across 7 languages and 4 model families. We further evaluate its effectiveness across 4 out-of-distribution languages and 4 additional datasets. We show that SEDATE achieves substantially superior safety scores across all languages and models over the best-performing baseline while retaining the general capabilities and incurring negligible overhead. Our results are robust, with the trends remaining similar for out-of-distribution languages and datasets.

Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
吃掉你的精度：基于评分标准的强化学习中精度目标缓解奖励欺骗问题
Rubric-based rewards enable effective reinforcement learning on non-verifiable tasks. However, because these rewards are typically defined as a weighted measure of rubric coverage, models are trained primarily to maximize a recall objective. As a result, RL-trained models produce responses that are more complete but also more verbose and contain more unnecessary or factually incorrect content, leading them to be less preferred than responses from the base model. To address this issue, we present the FORK reward, which jointly optimizes recall and a novel precision objective, which requires each unit of a model response to be both necessary and factually correct, as measured by rubric-driven necessity credits and a factual-correctness grader, respectively. Our experimental results show that FORK outperforms existing rubric-based RL methods and achieves Pareto-optimal performance that balances rubric coverage and overall response quality. Compared to the original recall-based reward, FORK substantially improves precision and reduces response length while achieving similar rubric coverage, which leads to significantly higher win rate compared to the base policy (e.g., from 10.6% to 68.0% on RubricHub-Medical and from 22.1% to 74.1% on HealthBench).

基于评分标准的奖励机制可在不可验证任务上实现有效的强化学习。然而，由于这些奖励通常定义为评分覆盖度的加权度量，模型主要被训练以最大化召回率目标。结果，强化学习训练出的模型生成的回答更完整但更冗长，包含更多不必要的或事实错误的内容，导致其不如基础模型生成的回答受青睐。为解决此问题，我们提出FORK奖励，该奖励联合优化召回率和一种新颖的精度目标，要求模型回答中的每个单元都必须必要且事实正确，分别通过评分驱动的必要性评分和事实正确性评分器来衡量。实验结果表明，FORK优于现有的基于评分标准的强化学习方法，并实现了在评分覆盖度与整体回答质量之间平衡的帕累托最优性能。相较于原始的召回率奖励，FORK显著提升了精度并减少了回答长度，同时保持相似的评分覆盖度，从而在与基础策略的对比中大幅提高胜率（例如，在RubricHub-Medical上从10.6%提升至68.0%，在HealthBench上从22.1%提升至74.1%）。

Small Edits, Shifting Decisions: Benchmarking LLM Accuracy and Reliability on French Input Variants
微小修改，决策变化：评估大语言模型在法语输入变体下的准确性和可靠性
French users may omit apostrophes and diacritics or make keyboard typos in everyday input. The effects of these common variations on language model performance and prediction reliability remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we construct a controlled French surface-variant benchmark covering seven task types, with 4,200 original-low-high triplets (12,600 input instances). Each high-intensity variant retains all low-intensity edits and adds further changes. We evaluate six models from two LLM families. The results show that accuracy decreases and Brier score and negative log-likelihood (NLL) increase with perturbation intensity. Larger models show smaller accuracy losses under high intensity, but increases in Brier score and NLL do not consistently decrease with scale. Keyboard typos cause the largest losses in accuracy and the quality of predicted probabilities at the predefined high-intensity settings. Finally, calibration temperatures fitted on original inputs transfer effectively to surface variants. Combining calibration with input restoration further improves Brier score and NLL over either method alone while preserving restored accuracy. Our benchmark provides a unified framework for jointly evaluating task accuracy and prediction reliability under common French surface variations.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support research idea generation and scientific discovery. Multi-agent debate offers a collaborative approach to this task by bringing together diverse perspectives to develop research ideas. However, a key challenge is how to equip agents with distinct and meaningful expertise to guide their contributions. Inspired by how researchers draw on accumulated research experience during collaboration, we introduce InsightAgents, a framework that constructs literature-grounded agent expertise by distilling insights from graphs of related papers. Guided by insights that trace evolving research approaches, reveal underlying assumptions, and identify unresolved challenges, within a line of research, agents jointly identify a research problem and propose, challenge, and refine potential approaches through debate to develop a research proposal. We evaluate InsightAgents against three research idea generation frameworks on 100 NLP research topics through pairwise comparisons by two LLM judges. In both online and offline knowledge settings, InsightAgents achieves the highest average score across the five evaluation dimensions under both judges.

We developed MARCA (Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Causality Assessment), a four-agent framework for Naranjo-based assessment, and evaluated agreement with human experts and exploratory differences between non-RAG and RAG-labelled scores. Methods: MARCA combined scientific literature retrieval, drug-label assessment, objective-evidence classification, and clinical causality reasoning using Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2. Agent-generated rationales informed human-assisted scoring. A consensus expert reference standard covered 215 ICSRs and 1,562 drug-event combinations (DECs) from FAERS (Q1-Q2 2025). Agreement was measured using percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa. Results: Question-level agreement was 96.8% for Naranjo Q2 (kappa = 0.491; 95% CI 0.265-0.663), 85.4% for Q5 (kappa = 0.269; 95% CI 0.180-0.340), and 96.8% for Q10 (kappa = 0.922; 95% CI 0.885-0.951). Final causality classification agreement was 79.4% (95% CI 71.8-85.3; kappa = 0.587, 95% CI 0.450-0.690). In a retrospective subset of 60 DECs, agreement was higher for RAG-labelled than non-RAG scores for Q5 (83.3% vs 65.0%) and Q10 (100.0% vs 18.3%). Discussion: MARCA-assisted assessment showed substantial variation in agreement across Naranjo questions, with lower concordance for alternative causes. Retrospective RAG comparisons are exploratory and do not establish prospective effectiveness.

Two Uncertainties Are Not One: Disagreement versus Decision-Risk in Cheap Structured Content Moderation
两种不确定性并非同一回事：廉价结构化内容审核中的分歧与决策风险
Content moderation compresses a graded, contested human judgment into a binary act (leave up / take down) over billions of items, at a scale where running a frontier LLM on every post is uneconomical. A new class of frozen "System One" models returns typed, calibrated decisions instead of text at ~USD 0.000025 per call and ~100 ms. We run the first independent audit of one such model on 142,658 human-labeled comments, and benchmark it against 14 frontier reasoning models (the GPT-5.x, Claude, Gemini 3, and Grok families) on a shared probe set. Two findings stand out. First, the cheap model is accuracy-competitive: its zero-shot classification AUROC (0.83) is not statistically separable (paired bootstrap, n=56; a failure to reject parity, not proof of equivalence) from 13 of the 14 frontier systems while costing 1-3 orders of magnitude less, and it is no worse calibrated than several of them. Second, "confidence" conflates two uncertainties that come apart: human disagreement (where annotators split on satire and coded language) and decision risk (where the automatic action is costly-wrong). Under an asymmetric moderation loss these call for opposite escalation signals, so no single confidence number serves both. Because the model prices extra questions at nearly zero, decomposing the judgment into parallel sub-questions and reading their spread recovers a human-disagreement signal that the model's native confidence misses -- but this remedy is specific: it helps the weakest, disagreement-blind models and only when the decomposition aligns with the sources of disagreement; a specialist toxicity model and the strongest LLMs do not need it, and the effect is distribution-sensitive. We will release the instrument, the cached runs, and the analysis.
中文翻译
内容审核需将大量分级且存在争议的人类判断压缩为二元操作（保留或删除），在亿级规模下，对每条评论运行前沿大模型成本过高。一类新型冻结的“系统一”模型以约0.000025美元/次和约100毫秒的代价返回类型化、校准后的决策，而非文本。我们首次独立审计了此类模型在142,658条人工标注评论上的表现，并将其与14个前沿推理模型（GPT-5.x、Claude、Gemini 3、Grok系列）在共享探测集上进行基准对比。两个发现尤为突出：第一，该廉价模型具备竞争力的准确率——其零样本分类AUROC（0.83）与14个前沿系统中的13个无统计差异（配对bootstrap检验，n=56；未能拒绝等效假设，非等效证明），且成本低1-3个数量级，其校准程度也不逊于其中多个模型。第二，“置信度”混淆了两种可分离的不确定性：人类分歧（标注者对讽刺和编码语言意见不一）与决策风险（自动操作代价高昂地出错）。在不对称审核损失下，二者需要相反的升级信号，因此单一置信度数值无法同时满足两者。由于该模型额外提问几乎无成本，将判断分解为并行子问题并分析其分布，可恢复模型原生置信度所缺失的人类分歧信号——但此方法具有特定适用性：仅对最弱、缺乏分歧感知能力的模型有效，且仅当分解方式与分歧来源一致时才有效；专业毒性模型和最强LLM无需此方法，且效果受数据分布影响敏感。我们将发布工具、缓存运行结果和分析。

LLM agents take instructions from the operator, repository configuration, user, tool results and saved memory, which often conflict. Instruction-hierarchy benchmarks ask whether the higher-ranked source wins, but a source sets position, role and label at once. First, we build WhoWins, 1,080 code-scored scenarios in five task types, each with up to five mutually exclusive instructions, and seven controlled experiments that vary only how instructions are delivered. Second, we study 14 open-weight models (0.6B to 122B, thinking off and on) over 1,887,356 scored replies, checking main findings on held-out scenarios. Inside one message the first of two conflicting lines wins 72.42 to 94.66%, and across messages it keeps 22.95 to 62.65%. A policy sent first in the system (or developer) message loses most conflicts with later lines in every Qwen model but wins most on gpt-oss when it acts. In tool and file-write tasks it wins less often than the same text sent first as a labelled user message, in every model-mode. Third, we test whether pairs forecast larger conflicts; forecasts improve in every model-mode once they know where the task line is. Finally, by our keyword patterns at most 2.92% of decided pair replies flag or hedge a conflict.

EviGround-CT: Sentence-to-Volume Grounding for Verifying LLM-Generated Chest CT Reports
EviGround-CT：用于验证LLM生成胸部CT报告的句子到体积定位
Chest computed tomography (CT) reports generated by large language models (LLMs) can describe positive findings that lack localized evidence in the scan. We propose EviGround-CT to verify these findings after report generation. A deterministic extractor identifies positive finding sentences, and a 3D grounding model predicts an evidence mask for each sentence. Using the full sentence retains anatomical location, laterality, and descriptive modifiers in the grounding query. We evaluate report generation on CT-RATE, and grounding and verification on a held-out 100-case ReXGroundingCT subset. Using the available annotations, sentence-grounded verification raises evidence-supported precision (ESP) from 0.263 to 0.365 across 137 extracted in-scope positives, compared with category conditioning. The corresponding unsupported positive finding rate falls from 0.737 to 0.635. The paired case-level bootstrap ESP difference is +0.102 (95% confidence interval: [0.028, 0.181]). The predicted masks associate individual report statements with spatial evidence that can be inspected alongside the CT.

A Benchmark for Controllable Speaking-Style Captioning in Audio-Language Models
音频-语言模型中可控说话风格字幕生成的基准测试
Speaking-style captioning (SSC) aims to generate natural language descriptions of how speech is delivered, capturing paralinguistic attributes such as vocal timbre, prosody, and expressivity. Many downstream applications, including conversational AI agents, controllable speech generation, and large-scale audio annotation, require dimension-specific style captions that describe targeted aspects of speech (e.g., speaker traits, emotion, or delivery style), rather than a single undifferentiated description. However, existing work lacks a unified formulation for controllable speaking-style captioning. We address this gap by formulating SSC as an instruction-following audio-language task, where explicit instructions specify the speaking-style dimensions to be described. We introduce StyleInstructCaps, the first standardized benchmark for controllable speaking-style captioning in audio-language models. StyleInstructCaps provides a dataset and evaluation framework that measures metadata groundedness, hallucination, instruction-following ability, generalization to unseen instructions and audio datasets, and speaker-style consistency. Across nine state-of-the-art audio-language models, we find that strong instruction-following ability does not necessarily imply grounded speaking-style understanding, and that SSC-specific instruction-diverse training substantially improves groundedness, controllability, and speaker consistency.

The Social World Model Evaluation Gap
社会世界模型评估差距
A negotiation assistant can reach a good deal without accurately predicting the other person's response. We ask whether evaluations of social world models test that prediction directly. We audit 113 works published from 1999 to 2026. 9 primary evaluations measure a real person's response to an action selected by the system or experimenter. Only 2 also compare an explicit response forecast with that response. Their predictors use information available when the action is chosen, and the evaluated responses were excluded from fitting; both randomize the intervention. A separate full-text check of 25 language-model works finds no experiment meeting these conditions. The other evaluations test current-state inference, task success, or prediction from recorded actions. We propose a 1-step negotiation experiment that separates these questions. The findings describe the audited sample, not the prevalence of this evaluation gap across the field.
中文翻译
谈判助手可以在不准确预测对方反应的情况下达成良好协议。我们探讨社会世界模型的评估是否直接测试了这种预测能力。我们审计了1999年至2026年间发表的113项研究。其中9项主要评估由系统或实验者选择的动作对真实人的反应。仅有2项还比较了明确的反应预测与实际反应。这些预测器使用动作选择时可用的信息，且评估响应未用于拟合模型；两者均对干预进行了随机化处理。对25项语言模型相关工作的全文检查发现，没有实验满足这些条件。其他评估主要测试当前状态推断、任务成功性或从记录动作中进行预测。我们提出了一种一步式谈判实验，以区分这些问题。研究结果描述了被审计样本的情况，而非该评估差距在整个领域中的普遍程度。

Natural-language service intents in integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial (TN/NTN) 6G networks can be incomplete, ambiguous, or inconsistent, making unconstrained LLM generation challenging for reliable network-facing orchestration. This paper proposes a knowledge-guided LLM framework that combines grammar-constrained semantic parsing with a knowledge-graph (KG)-driven clarification loop to produce validated, orchestration-ready service profiles across four representative service classes. On a 200-sample intent dataset, the framework achieves 89% classification accuracy and 95% policy validity with an average of 0.66 clarification turns per request. Skill$^{\infty}$: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization
Skill$^{ ext{∞}}$：智能体技能优化的递归自我改进
Recursive self-improvement (RSI), in which a system also improves the way it improves, is a long-standing aspiration on the path to AGI. Language agents increasingly store procedural knowledge in reusable skills. Optimizing skills offers a direct way to achieve RSI, because the optimization procedure itself can be encoded as a skill. Existing skill optimizers, however, follow a hand-designed procedure. Even methods that evolve a meta-skill confine it to a fixed pipeline and relearn it for each task. We present Skill$^{\infty}$, which makes skill optimization recursively self-improving: a meta agent follows a meta-skill to optimize task skills and optimizes the meta-skill itself using the same procedure. The optimization is agent-led. The meta agent diagnoses execution traces, proposes candidates, requests independent reviews, and allocates the search budget. The meta-skill defines these steps, allowing self-improvement to rewrite them. This meta-skill is also decoupled from task skills, refined on multiple skill optimization tasks and then reused to optimize task skills across diverse domains. As in deployment, skills at both levels are standard packages loaded through native skill discovery. On 83 SkillsBench tasks, Skill$^{\infty}$ reaches a pass rate of 60.7%, compared with 56.4% for human-curated skills and 54.5% for SkillEvolver.
中文翻译
递归自我改进（RSI），即系统同时改进其改进方式，是通往通用人工智能（AGI）道路上长期追求的目标。语言智能体越来越多地将程序性知识存储为可复用的技能。优化技能是实现RSI的直接途径，因为优化过程本身可编码为一项技能。然而，现有技能优化器遵循人工设计流程。即使那些演化元技能的方法也局限于固定流水线，并为每个任务重新学习。我们提出Skill$^{ ext{∞}}$，使技能优化具备递归自我改进能力：一个元智能体遵循元技能来优化任务技能，并使用相同流程优化元技能自身。该优化由智能体主导：元智能体诊断执行轨迹，提出候选方案，请求独立评审，并分配搜索预算。元技能定义这些步骤，允许自我改进重写它们。该元技能还与任务技能解耦，在多个技能优化任务上精炼后，再复用于跨不同领域的任务技能优化。如同部署阶段，两个层级的技能均为标准包，通过原生技能发现加载。在83个SkillsBench任务上，Skill$^{ ext{∞}}$达到60.7%的通过率，优于人工标注技能的56.4%和SkillEvolver的54.5%。

The Voice on the Line
线路中的声音
A transcriber listening through one microphone also hears everyone near it. We train causal voice isolators: masking transformers of 140M, 243M and 374M parameters, 20 ms of latency, enrolling the caller from the call itself. Short evaluation windows hide two failures that real calls expose: forgetting the caller when another voice talks alone for a while, and damaging a caller who is alone. Long calls with turns, memory beyond the attention window, real headset crosstalk and drifting caller levels address both, but each trades one against the other. WavLM-Large's own weights, made causal and trained with the model, move the trade: M with them (555M parameters) lowers the error on our development sets from 11.44% to 10.55%; a student trained from scratch to imitate WavLM does not, and w2v-BERT 2.0 and Whisper's encoder, pre-trained on far more audio, help less or not at all. A lone caller loses most at the start of a recording: no training call opened with someone already talking. Training on windows cut from longer calls lowers the error on clean development calls from 3.92% to 2.96%; this is our release. Live, the release makes 16.13% word errors on 60 s AMI windows, against 23.66% for VoxLock, the strongest open isolator, and 10.19% on its own AMI windows, against 11.71%; it is level on Krisp's benchmark (5.74% against 5.63%), and a caller who is alone still loses more words than with VoxLock (5.58% against 2.92% on clean test calls). Distilled into 22.1M parameters without WavLM, it runs live on one CPU thread inside a LiveKit agent, at 33% of a core per call in 20 ms frames, with 10.66% error on our development sets (the release 10.49%). We open-source the release and this CPU model, with a LiveKit plugin, at https://huggingface.co/collections/Scicom-intl/voice-isolator.

Improving VLMs on Scientific Chart Analysis via Autonomous Evolution

Understanding and operating with scientific charts is a standard approach in data analysis, and while humans are good at interpreting such charts, open vision-language models (VLMs) are known to perform poorly when it comes to question answering based on such data types. Motivated by an initial observation that many of their errors are due to inexact answering, we raise the following natural question: how much accuracy can we recover without changing the model at all? In this paper, we study this question by searching over inference programs and the code around a "frozen" version of the model. Using ideas from autonomous evolution (famously used in AlphaEvolve), we first start from a baseline inference program, and in each round we show an LLM judge the code together with a few failures on training questions, and ask for an improving evolutionary move. As usual in autonomous evolution approaches, the candidate programs are kept in a small pool ranked by training accuracy, and the next edit is performed on top-scorers from this pool. We run this approach on three VLMs and four popular benchmarks on scientific charts, and we measure the fraction of descriptive questions whose answer exactly matches the ground truth. The accuracy improves in all experimental settings. On average, it rises from 16.6% with the starting program to 41.3% with the evolved one, and the largest single increase is 55.2 percentage points. As a side benefit, our evolved program is 3.8x faster than the starting program, because short answers are easier to grade and faster to generate. Our results demonstrate that a large part of the observed errors arise due to the inference pipeline, and that optimizing it can improve the "frozen" VLM without the need to retrain it.

Reinforcement Learning Done Right for Explicit Confidence Targets
为明确置信度目标正确地进行强化学习
Large language models (LLMs) can produce plausible but incorrect answers when they are uncertain, which can mislead users and undermine model reliability. Training models to abstain with reinforcement learning is a natural approach, but most existing methods use a fixed error penalty and therefore cannot adapt their behavior to different confidence requirements at inference time. We study \emph{explicit confidence targets}, where a user specifies a target \(p\) in the prompt and the model directly chooses whether to answer or abstain, with the goal of achieving an accuracy of at least \(p\) among answered questions. However, learning to respond to different confidence targets with a single model has proven difficult, and prior attempts have failed to distinguish different targets. We show that this failure comes from two problems: the reward signal that distinguishes different values of $p$ is often lost during optimization, while the original error penalty grows without bound as $p$ approaches one. We propose RLEC (\textbf{R}einforcement \textbf{L}earning with \textbf{E}xplicit \textbf{C}onfidence Targets), which preserves the learning signal needed to distinguish confidence targets, introduces a stable reward family that keeps the desired answer condition unchanged, and uses reward scheduling to balance effective learning and training stability. Together, these designs enable the first successful training of a single LLM for explicit confidence target control. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks and model scales show that RLEC largely preserves general capabilities and achieves competitive calibration performance. RLEC also supports fine-grained target control without an external decision system or threshold calibration after training. By making explicit confidence targets part of the trained policy, RLEC opens a new and more direct path toward behavioral calibration.

Objective: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare has opened new possibilities for AI-assisted clinical decision-making; however, safe and effective deployment remains challenging because of hallucination and domain misalignment. This study introduces DocTalk, a doctor-assistive question-answering (QA) system designed to generate concise, chart-grounded responses from de-identified discharge summaries. Methods: We developed a high-fidelity data generation pipeline that produces 500 clinically relevant QA pairs through sentence-level decomposition, chain-of-thought-guided question formulation, and expert review.
