Multilingual BabyLM systems usually fix language sampling proportions even though the weakest language can change during training. We present ARMOR-DP, a modular framework that diagnoses imbalance arising from representation, exposure, capacity, and objective pressure, and uses per-language validation loss to update sampling. Controlled experiments show that equal character budgets create a severe representation artifact for Chinese; byte-level encoding removes much of it, while static Chinese protection can subsequently make English the weakest language. The dynamic controller tracks these transitions and achieves a better score--balance tradeoff than fixed protection. On official evaluation, curriculum-dynamic checkpoints outperform a matched static Chinese-protective baseline while using fewer Chinese epochs; scaling capacity yields the strongest internal ARMOR-DP system. These results support a simple conclusion: multilingual weakness is a training-time state rather than a fixed property of a language. ARMOR-DP therefore separates diagnosis from intervention, allowing protection to follow the current bottleneck instead of a predetermined language label.

Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents

Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. Even successful interactions may underrepresent multi-step dependencies or contain actions that are unjustified by the information visible to the agent at decision time. We identify two coupled requirements for effective trajectory supervision: compositional coverage, so that important observation-action dependencies are represented, and decision grounding, so that each supervised action is supported by the learner-visible interaction history. We introduce Trajectory2Gym, which constructs executable interactions around under-supported compositional structures and derives supervision only from grounded decisions in their realized executions. Structural-support selection allocates the resulting experience, while parent-normalized supervised fine-tuning preserves the semantic interaction as the unit of training weight. This reframes trajectory generation as the deliberate construction of learnable interaction experience, rather than the collection of successful trajectories. Across five Qwen3 scales, Trajectory2Gym improves Tau1, Tau2, and BFCL at every tested scale, increasing the equal-weight three-benchmark mean by 16.9-29.8 percentage points. The gains are strongest in stateful and multi-turn interaction, where later decisions depend on earlier observations and feedback. Our results suggest that scaling tool-use agents depends not only on collecting more successful trajectories, but on constructing interactions whose dependencies are represented and whose decisions are learnable from the agent's visible history.

As the applications of AI continue to expand across various multimodal and multilingual domains, ensuring safe and responsible deployment of these systems has become an important concern. A wide-range of interventions have been proposed to make AI responses safer and more reliable. They often incur substantial computational or annotation costs, or cannot be extended to multilingual settings. In this work, we propose Selective Detection And Targeted Editing (SEDATE), a training-free approach based on detect-edit-verify strategy. SEDATE first detects the responsible neurons, edits them as and when necessary and finally verifies the model responses; all without any additional model training. We evaluate SEDATE across 7 languages and 4 model families. We further evaluate its effectiveness across 4 out-of-distribution languages and 4 additional datasets. We show that SEDATE achieves substantially superior safety scores across all languages and models over the best-performing baseline while retaining the general capabilities and incurring negligible overhead. Our results are robust, with the trends remaining similar for out-of-distribution languages and datasets.

一个模型，两条路径：平衡语言模型的单次通过与循环推理性能
Repeating Transformer layers can improve language-model performance without adding parameters. A pretrained model can be adapted to support both single-pass and looped inference by reusing middle-layer weights for additional computation. Because both paths share weights, training to improve looped predictions can degrade single-pass quality. We study joint training strategies using weighted losses on both outputs, with guidance from the frozen original model. Joint supervision substantially reduces single-pass degradation compared to looped-only training, while preserving looped gains over ordinary continued training. Most of this benefit comes from adjusting the single-pass loss weight, with guidance from the frozen original model further improving the looped output. With validation-selected weights, our method preserves single-pass quality within a predefined tolerance of ordinary continued training while improving looped predictions.

Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
吃掉你的精度：基于评分标准的强化学习中精度目标缓解奖励欺骗问题
Rubric-based rewards enable effective reinforcement learning on non-verifiable tasks. However, because these rewards are typically defined as a weighted measure of rubric coverage, models are trained primarily to maximize a recall objective. As a result, RL-trained models produce responses that are more complete but also more verbose and contain more unnecessary or factually incorrect content, leading them to be less preferred than responses from the base model. To address this issue, we present the FORK reward, which jointly optimizes recall and a novel precision objective, which requires each unit of a model response to be both necessary and factually correct, as measured by rubric-driven necessity credits and a factual-correctness grader, respectively. Our experimental results show that FORK outperforms existing rubric-based RL methods and achieves Pareto-optimal performance that balances rubric coverage and overall response quality. Compared to the original recall-based reward, FORK substantially improves precision and reduces response length while achieving similar rubric coverage, which leads to significantly higher win rate compared to the base policy (e.g., from 10.6% to 68.0% on RubricHub-Medical and from 22.1% to 74.1% on HealthBench).

Towards a Learnable Retriever for Textual Graph Question Answering
迈向可学习的检索器：面向文本图问答的任务
Textual graph question answering (GraphQA) and graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) have gained increasing attention as a way to ground large language models (LLMs) on structured knowledge. Despite extensive efforts, existing methods still face two key gaps. The first is an architectural gap: existing methods typically fine-tune an LLM-based generator, but do not also make the retriever itself a learnable LLM for graph evidence selection within one end-to-end retrieve-then-generate pipeline. The second is a retrieval-supervision gap: existing retrievers rarely use gold answer signals to supervise evidence selection. As a result, they may fail to recall evidence nodes required for reasoning, resulting in insufficient coverage of the gold answer set; meanwhile, naive attempts to boost recall often introduce excessive irrelevant information that compromises compactness and overwhelms the LLM. To address these gaps, we propose TaLenT, an LLM-based end-to-end retriever-generator framework for textual GraphQA. To bridge the architectural gap, TaLenT pairs a learnable LLM-based retriever for evidence selection with a fine-tuned LLM-based generator within one unified retrieve-then-generate pipeline. To bridge the retrieval-supervision gap, we leverage gold answer signals as retriever supervision. Specifically, we stratify graph nodes into gold answers, answer-related nodes, and irrelevant noise. We then adopt a weighted pseudo-label loss to prioritize gold answers and preserve answer-related nodes for coverage, while discarding irrelevant noise for compactness. Experimental results across three GraphQA datasets demonstrate that TaLenT consistently improves downstream performance.

文本图问答（GraphQA）和基于图的检索增强生成（GraphRAG）作为将大语言模型（LLM）锚定在结构化知识上的方式，正受到越来越多关注。尽管已有大量努力，现有方法仍存在两个关键差距。第一是架构差距：现有方法通常微调基于LLM的生成器，但未使检索器本身也成为可学习的LLM，以在端到端的检索-生成流程中完成图证据选择。第二是检索监督差距：现有检索器很少利用真实答案信号来监督证据选择。因此，它们可能无法召回推理所需的证据节点，导致对真实答案集的覆盖不足；同时，简单提升召回率常引入过多无关信息，损害简洁性并压垮LLM。为解决这些差距，我们提出TaLenT，一种基于LLM的端到端检索-生成框架，用于文本图问答。为弥合架构差距，TaLenT在统一的检索-生成管道中，将可学习的LLM检索器与微调的LLM生成器配对。为弥合检索监督差距，我们利用真实答案信号作为检索器的监督。具体而言，我们将图节点分为真实答案、相关节点和无关噪声三类，并采用加权伪标签损失，优先保留真实答案并维持相关节点覆盖，同时丢弃无关噪声以保证简洁性。在三个GraphQA数据集上的实验结果表明，TaLenT持续提升了下游性能。

Large language models (LLMs) are reported to be susceptible to reliability issues including hallucinations and reasoning errors. Existing quality detectors can predict unreliable outputs based on internal representations with decent accuracies. However, training these detectors often requires substantial domain-specific labeled data, which limits their applicability to new domains. We propose to address this challenge by transferring representational signatures across related domains. More specifically, we build a statistical framework that first extracts low-dimensional signatures for each domain, then uses cross-fitting to learn composition weights of domain-specific predictors. The weights adapt to each source domain's predictive relevance to the target domain. Our asymptotic analysis of a least-squares analogue characterizes the limiting prediction risk and aggregation weights in terms of domain discrepancies and representation bias. Experiments across multiple hallucination datasets and open-weight LLMs show that, with only 25 labeled questions in the new domain, adaptive transfer improves hallucination-detection AUROC by 6.8%. A selected-set case study identifies contrasting clean-margin profiles among the examples exchanged by the two rules, while a full-pool ablation shows that entropy prefiltering is not uniformly beneficial. These retrospective results characterize the empirical utility and limitations of perturbation-based selection under a fixed adaptation protocol. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support research idea generation and scientific discovery. Multi-agent debate offers a collaborative approach to this task by bringing together diverse perspectives to develop research ideas. However, a key challenge is how to equip agents with distinct and meaningful expertise to guide their contributions. Inspired by how researchers draw on accumulated research experience during collaboration, we introduce InsightAgents, a framework that constructs literature-grounded agent expertise by distilling insights from graphs of related papers. Guided by insights that trace evolving research approaches, reveal underlying assumptions, and identify unresolved challenges, within a line of research, agents jointly identify a research problem and propose, challenge, and refine potential approaches through debate to develop a research proposal. We evaluate InsightAgents against three research idea generation frameworks on 100 NLP research topics through pairwise comparisons by two LLM judges. In both online and offline knowledge settings, InsightAgents achieves the highest average score across the five evaluation dimensions under both judges.

The Emergence and Sparsification of a Syntactic Circuit

To understand the emergence of grammatical behavior in language models, we track circuits for subject-verb number agreement in pythia-1b and ten seeds of pythia-410m across training. We find that subject-verb agreement is learned early, and is initially handled by a diffuse collection of neurons. However, after agreement behavior has stabilized, the mechanisms responsible for it continue to reorganize. The attention heads which mediate agreement often shift during training: in the case of pythia-1b, behavior is controlled by two heads early in training but by a third (different) head later. Furthermore, the circuit shrinks over training, with pythia-1b's final circuit being strikingly sparse. We take these results to be informative about how linguistic knowledge emerges and is represented in a language model.

FlexA-Mem: Budget-Adaptive Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
FlexA-Mem：面向大语言模型智能体的预算自适应代理记忆
Large language model (LLM) agents work in scenarios with very different memory needs. A question about past conversations needs the exact facts it names, while a multi-step task needs a trace of the steps already taken together with details that the next step cannot name. Existing memories are each designed and tested for one kind of scenario. Retrieval memories such as A-Mem miss steps that the current query does not express, summaries drop exact strings, and pairing the two fixes the split of the budget in advance. We propose FlexA-Mem, a general memory that writes each unit of history once into an immutable store and renders a fresh memory for every call. The rendered memory is a compact timeline of records plus detail that a fixed rule fits into the remaining room without an LLM call. The detail is either relevant units as raw text or excerpts or the verbatim pieces that best match the query. With one store, FlexA-Mem serves both kinds of scenario. On AppWorld challenge tasks at 4k, it outperforms the second-best method by 11.5%, and on 147 unused tasks with predictions fixed in advance it outperforms A-Mem with a summary by 12.2%. On LongMemEval and LoCoMo, it matches a dedicated keyword retriever that writes no memory, while memories built on text written by an LLM fall far behind at tight budgets. Ablations show that the timeline carries AppWorld completion, whereas recovery mainly saves steps there and decides accuracy on exact facts. Code is available at https://github.com/WujiangXu/Flex-Amem
中文翻译
大型语言模型（LLM）智能体在不同场景下具有差异极大的记忆需求。例如，关于过去对话的问题需要精确的事实，而多步骤任务则需要已执行步骤的完整轨迹及下一步无法表达的细节。现有记忆机制针对特定场景设计并测试，如检索式记忆（如A-Mem）会遗漏当前查询未体现的步骤，摘要会丢失精确字符串，而将两者结合则提前固定了预算分配。我们提出FlexA-Mem，一种通用记忆系统：将每条历史记录写入一次不可变存储，并为每次调用生成一份全新的记忆。生成的记忆包含紧凑的时间线记录和细节，这些细节由固定规则填入剩余空间，无需额外LLM调用。细节可为相关单元的原始文本或摘录，或最匹配查询的原文片段。一个统一存储即可满足两类场景需求。在AppWorld挑战任务中（4k上下文），其性能优于次优方法11.5%；在147个未使用任务上（预测提前固定），优于带摘要的A-Mem 12.2%。在LongMemEval和LoCoMo基准上，其表现媲美专用关键词检索器（不写入记忆），而基于LLM生成文本构建的记忆在高预算限制下明显落后。消融实验表明，时间线对AppWorld任务完成度起关键作用，而恢复机制主要节省步骤并决定精确事实的准确性。代码已开源。

Each Insufficient in Its Own Way: Calibrating Language Models Across Varying Evidence States
各有所不足：在不同证据状态下的语言模型校准
How can a language model know whether it has enough evidence to answer? Language models tend to answer even when the evidence they have is insufficient. Deciding whether to answer or gather more evidence requires a calibrated estimate of how likely an answer is to be correct with the available evidence. However, most calibration work treats the input as fixed, without asking how this estimate should change with the evidence. We introduce \emph{evidence-state calibration}, which requires a model's confidence before answering to match its probability of answering correctly and to change accordingly whenever the evidence changes this probability. We propose \ours{} (\textbf{Suffi}ciency \textbf{C}onfidence \textbf{E}stimation), which fine-tunes the confidence already present in a model's next-token distribution to match how often the model answers correctly from each evidence state. Across clinical diagnosis and multi-hop question answering with four models from two families, \ours{} reduces the Brier score by up to 60\% and increases AUROC by up to 0.16. Its confidence matches the empirical success rate and responds not only to the amount of evidence but also to which evidence is present, showing that models can learn to judge whether their current evidence is enough to answer.
中文翻译
语言模型如何判断自己是否拥有足够的证据来回答？目前的语言模型倾向于在证据不足时仍强行作答。决定是否回答或继续收集证据，需要对当前证据下答案正确的可能性进行校准估计。然而，大多数校准研究将输入视为固定不变，未探讨该估计应如何随证据变化。我们引入“证据状态校准”，要求模型在回答前的置信度与其正确回答的概率相匹配，并在证据变化时相应调整。我们提出 extbf{Suffi}ciency extbf{C}onfidence extbf{E}stimation（ extbf{SuffiCE}），通过微调模型自身下一词分布中的置信度，使其与从每个证据状态中正确回答的实际频率相匹配。在来自两个模型家族的四种模型上，针对临床诊断和多跳问答任务， extbf{SuffiCE}将Brier分数降低高达60%，AUROC提升最高达0.16。其置信度与实际成功率达到良好匹配，并不仅响应证据数量，还响应具体证据内容，表明模型可以学会判断当前证据是否足以作答。

LLM agents take instructions from the operator, repository configuration, user, tool results and saved memory, which often conflict. Instruction-hierarchy benchmarks ask whether the higher-ranked source wins, but a source sets position, role and label at once. First, we build WhoWins, 1,080 code-scored scenarios in five task types, each with up to five mutually exclusive instructions, and seven controlled experiments that vary only how instructions are delivered. Second, we study 14 open-weight models (0.6B to 122B, thinking off and on) over 1,887,356 scored replies, checking main findings on held-out scenarios. Inside one message the first of two conflicting lines wins 72.42 to 94.66%, and across messages it keeps 22.95 to 62.65%. A policy sent first in the system (or developer) message loses most conflicts with later lines in every Qwen model but wins most on gpt-oss when it acts. In tool and file-write tasks it wins less often than the same text sent first as a labelled user message, in every model-mode. Third, we test whether pairs forecast larger conflicts; forecasts improve in every model-mode once they know where the task line is. Finally, by our keyword patterns at most 2.92% of decided pair replies flag or hedge a conflict.

A Benchmark for Controllable Speaking-Style Captioning in Audio-Language Models

Speaking-style captioning (SSC) aims to generate natural language descriptions of how speech is delivered, capturing paralinguistic attributes such as vocal timbre, prosody, and expressivity. Many downstream applications, including conversational AI agents, controllable speech generation, and large-scale audio annotation, require dimension-specific style captions that describe targeted aspects of speech (e.g., speaker traits, emotion, or delivery style), rather than a single undifferentiated description. However, existing work lacks a unified formulation for controllable speaking-style captioning. We address this gap by formulating SSC as an instruction-following audio-language task, where explicit instructions specify the speaking-style dimensions to be described. We introduce StyleInstructCaps, the first standardized benchmark for controllable speaking-style captioning in audio-language models. StyleInstructCaps provides a dataset and evaluation framework that measures metadata groundedness, hallucination, instruction-following ability, generalization to unseen instructions and audio datasets, and speaker-style consistency. Across nine state-of-the-art audio-language models, we find that strong instruction-following ability does not necessarily imply grounded speaking-style understanding, and that SSC-specific instruction-diverse training substantially improves groundedness, controllability, and speaker consistency.

Conceptizer: Next-Token Prediction Is Not All You Need
Conceptizer：下一个词预测并非全部所需
Next-token prediction (NTP) rewards only the token that occurs next, penalizing every alternative. But natural language often offers many ways to express the same meaning. We introduce Conceptizer, a training framework that extends next-token prediction with a reward for meaning. Conceptizer uses a fixed, model-agnostic vocabulary of ~9K concepts, built from contextual synonyms, as units of meaning alongside tokens as units of text. It maps each next-token distribution to a concept distribution and shares the reward for the target meaning across its possible wordings. This provides a concept-level training signal without adding model parameters. Applied to 3 model families at 1B-8B parameters, Conceptizer achieves the lowest held-out NTP perplexity at concept-target positions and assigns the highest probability to contextual synonyms, against all 3 baselines. It also improves downstream performance on knowledge and sentiment tasks while remaining comparable on commonsense. These results show that language models can be directly optimized to predict meaning, not just the next token.

Recursive Semantic Divergence for LLM Agent Consistency
基于递归语义分歧的LLM智能体一致性
Large Language Model (LLM) agents with tool use exhibit inconsistent behavior across independent runs from identical states, calling different tools, producing contradictory outputs, or pursuing divergent strategies. This variability compounds over time and undermines deployment reliability. Existing evaluation metrics primarily measure task correctness via completion-based scores and do not capture consistency in agent behavior across executions. Separately, agent behavior is analyzed either at the token level using probability distributions or at the single-response level using semantic clustering, but neither captures how inconsistency propagates across future turns of a trajectory. We introduce Recursive Semantic Divergence (RSD), an unsupervised trajectory-level consistency metric adapted from bisimulation metrics in reinforcement learning. RSD measures the expected cumulative semantic disagreement between two independent rollouts of the same agent from the same state, using natural language inference to detect logical inconsistency. It is defined recursively over future states and approximated by a neural network trained on independent rollouts. The learned metric estimates future divergence from the current state, providing a consistency score at each turn without requiring the full trajectory to complete. When used as a reward signal for fine-tuning, RSD reduces the variation in task progress from 132% to 91% on tau2-bench and from 90% to 44% on toolsandbox, while improving performance across benchmarks and model scales. Training with RSD as an additional reward signal matches supervised fine-tuning performance with substantially lower variance, without requiring ground-truth labels.

To bridge this gap, we design energy-steered models (ESMs) for foundational language modeling. ESMs integrate energy steering and token generation within a single architecture to leverage the energy-guided search to refine token generation. Specifically, ESMs first optimize a latent state over the energy landscape, then leverages the refined latent state for token generation. By performing such energy-guided pre-training on large-scale corpora, ESMs learn generally effective energy landscape where favorable tokens correspond to lower energy values. To explore the scaling behavior of ESMs, we pre-train ESMs on three large-scale corpora, then evaluate across 26 downstream tasks spanning a broad range of domains. Our results demonstrate that ESMs have promising scaling behaviors with increasing model size and training data, and outperform GPTs on most downstream tasks. These findings highlight ESMs as a promising architecture for large-scale pre-training and general purpose problem solving. We fully release the model weights and training infrastructure to enable the community to completely reproduce and extend our results. Center-of-Mass Interpretation of Evolution Strategies
进化策略的质心解释
Evolution strategies (ES) update a model by sampling a population of perturbed copies, scoring each one, and moving in the reward-weighted direction of the perturbations. This update is usually presented as an estimate of a smoothed gradient. We present a geometrical interpretation of this update instead. Treat each perturbed model as a particle and its reward as the particle's mass. Before scoring, every particle has the same mass and the population balances at its centroid. Once rewards are assigned, it balances at its reward-weighted center of mass instead. We show that the mean-subtracted ES update is exactly this displacement, scaled by a scalar factor that depends on the mean reward, for any finite population. The physical reading needs nonnegative rewards, which can always be arranged by adding a constant to every reward without changing the update. In the limit of a large population or under antithetic sampling, the centroid sits on the model itself, so ES has an even simpler geometric interpretation: from its current location, the model moves towards the reward-weighted center of mass of its own population. The same picture explains what subtracting the mean reward does: it changes the point from which the displacement is measured, from the model to the sampled centroid. Our contribution is an intuitive, geometric way to visualize an ES update, exact for any finite population.
中文翻译
进化策略（ES）通过采样一组扰动副本，评分每个副本，并沿奖励加权方向移动来更新模型。该更新通常被表述为平滑梯度的估计。本文提出了该更新的几何解释。将每个扰动模型视为粒子，其奖励视为粒子质量。在评分前，每个粒子质量相同，群体平衡于其质心。评分后，群体平衡于其奖励加权的质心。我们证明，减去均值后的 ES 更新恰好等于该位移，缩放因子取决于平均奖励，适用于任意有限群体。该物理解读要求非负奖励，可通过为所有奖励添加常数实现，而不改变更新。在大群体极限或采用反向采样时，质心位于模型自身位置，因此 ES 具有更简单的几何解释：模型从当前位置移动到其自身群体的奖励加权质心。同一图景也解释了减去平均奖励的作用：它改变了位移的测量起点，从模型本身变为采样质心。我们的贡献是为任意有限群体提供了一种直观且精确的几何可视化方式来理解 ES 更新。

We study how to apply error-targeted learning to terminal agents, which solve long-horizon tasks specified in natural language by interacting with a command shell. Existing error-targeted methods are designed for single-turn tasks, and existing analyses of agent failures are used to evaluate and debug agents rather than to train them. MiRL then trains the policy with RL, starting rollouts at the steps where these misbehaviors occur and rewarding a rollout only if it passes the tests and avoids the misbehavior. On Qwen3.5-4B, eight misbehaviors account for 52.1% of wrong steps. After training with MiRL, the policy repeats the measured misbehaviors 43% to 57% less often on average on unseen prefixes. MiRL outperforms TMax-4B on Terminal-Bench Lite (51.8% vs. 47.4%) and matches it on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (21.3% vs. 20.6%), while using 35% of its rollouts. These results show that error-targeted learning can be applied to realistic, long-horizon terminal tasks.

Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models
整合奖励，而非采样它：全双工语音模型中中断与回应信号的窗口似然
A full-duplex spoken dialogue model must yield when the user cuts in and hold when the user merely backchannels. Sequence-level RL with a timing reward (GRPO) is the usual recipe; we test its whole-rollout form on four open models and find two failures. A binary window reward gives zero advantage on exactly the windows that most need learning (a zero-gradient trap), and the one score per rollout is spread over listening-state decisions the reward is not written in terms of (credit leakage), so the model talks into silence or stops answering. Both come from sampling a reward that is a known function of a few binary control decisions. We propose \emph{window likelihood} (\WL): sample a continuation per window, but integrate in closed form over the stop decisions it visits and maximise the log-probability of acting correctly---a noisy-OR for yielding, a survival product for holding. On HumDial-FDBench, \WL\ gives the best yield/hold F1 on all six structurally different open models we post-train, exceeds Kyutai's released GRPO checkpoints (trained on different data), and adds no re-opening of the floor on any model.

全双工语音对话模型必须在用户打断时让出发言权，在用户仅发出回应信号时保持沉默。通常采用基于时间奖励的序列级强化学习（GRPO）方法；我们对四个开源模型测试其完整回放形式，发现存在两种失败情况。二值窗口奖励在最需要学习的窗口上未能提供优势（零梯度陷阱），且每轮回放的单一得分被分散到与奖励无关的听觉状态决策中（信用泄漏），导致模型在沉默中说话或停止回答。这两种问题均源于对已知函数的奖励进行采样，该函数仅由少数二值控制决策决定。我们提出 extit{窗口似然}（ ext{WL}）：每窗口采样一个延续，但以闭式积分方式对访问的停止决策进行整合，并最大化正确行为的对数概率——一种用于让出发言权的噪声或逻辑，以及用于保持沉默的生存乘积。在HumDial-FDBench上， ext{WL}在所有六种结构不同的开源模型上均取得最佳的让出/保持F1分数，超越了Kyutai发布的GRPO检查点（在不同数据上训练），且未在任何模型上造成发言权重新开放。

S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning

Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training. Common alternatives lack token-level credit assignment and typically rely on grouped rollouts to estimate prompt-specific baselines. A critic can address both limitations, but long-CoT critic training is hindered by insufficient coverage of trajectories with diverse lengths and early gradients dominated by the newly initialized value head. We introduce S3AC (Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic) for LLM reasoning, built around a practical critic-training recipe. The trained critic provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines. Using the prompt-level baseline to estimate difficulty, we propose Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling (DAPS). DAPS combines this estimate with outcome history to select prompts before generation, reducing rollout waste without offline difficulty initialization. S3AC improves group-rollout performance across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, outperforming a modern GRPO variant (GRPO-X). At 35B, it sustains single-rollout training while tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.

GPDPO: Learning from Reward Conflicts via Group Pareto-Dominance Policy Optimization
GPDPO：通过组帕累托占优策略优化实现从奖励冲突中学习
Multi-reward reinforcement learning offers a promising framework for aligning large language models (LLMs) with diverse objectives, but conflicting reward signals can induce ambiguous update directions and hinder stable optimization. Existing approaches address such conflicts through reward reweighting, gradient coordination, or rollout filtering, yet they primarily operate on per-response or group-level optimization signals and underexploit relational information among sampled responses. As a result, conflict-filtered rollouts may still contain useful supervision that is discarded during training. We propose Group Pareto-Dominance Policy Optimization (GPDPO), a multi-reward policy optimization method that recovers pairwise supervision from conflict-filtered rollouts. GPDPO identifies Pareto-dominance relations among sampled responses and converts them into auxiliary preference signals, which are jointly optimized with the original policy objective. This enables more effective reuse of existing rollouts without additional sampling or reward evaluation. Experiments on API-Bank across multiple model scales and reward configurations show that GPDPO consistently outperforms competitive multi-reward optimization baselines. Further analysis demonstrates that GPDPO reduces both group-relative and pairwise reward conflicts, supporting the effectiveness of exploiting relational supervision for multi-reward alignment. Code will be released.

Language agents increasingly store procedural knowledge in reusable skills. Optimizing skills offers a direct way to achieve RSI, because the optimization procedure itself can be encoded as a skill. Existing skill optimizers, however, follow a hand-designed procedure. Even methods that evolve a meta-skill confine it to a fixed pipeline and relearn it for each task. We present Skill$^{\infty}$, which makes skill optimization recursively self-improving: a meta agent follows a meta-skill to optimize task skills and optimizes the meta-skill itself using the same procedure. The optimization is agent-led. The meta agent diagnoses execution traces, proposes candidates, requests independent reviews, and allocates the search budget. The meta-skill defines these steps, allowing self-improvement to rewrite them. This meta-skill is also decoupled from task skills, refined on multiple skill optimization tasks and then reused to optimize task skills across diverse domains. As in deployment, skills at both levels are standard packages loaded through native skill discovery. On 83 SkillsBench tasks, Skill$^{\infty}$ reaches a pass rate of 60.7%, compared with 56.4% for human-curated skills and 54.5% for SkillEvolver.

递归自我改进（RSI），即系统同时改进其改进方式，是通往通用人工智能（AGI）道路上长期追求的目标。语言智能体越来越多地将程序性知识存储为可复用的技能。优化技能是实现RSI的直接途径，因为优化过程本身可编码为一项技能。然而，现有技能优化器遵循人工设计流程。即使那些演化元技能的方法也局限于固定流水线，并为每个任务重新学习。我们提出Skill$^{ ext{∞}}$，使技能优化具备递归自我改进能力：一个元智能体遵循元技能来优化任务技能，并使用相同流程优化元技能自身。该优化由智能体主导：元智能体诊断执行轨迹，提出候选方案，请求独立评审，并分配搜索预算。元技能定义这些步骤，允许自我改进重写它们。该元技能还与任务技能解耦，在多个技能优化任务上精炼后，再复用于跨不同领域的任务技能优化。如同部署阶段，两个层级的技能均为标准包，通过原生技能发现加载。在83个SkillsBench任务上，Skill$^{ ext{∞}}$达到60.7%的通过率，优于人工标注技能的56.4%和SkillEvolver的54.5%。

The Voice on the Line
线路中的声音
A transcriber listening through one microphone also hears everyone near it. We train causal voice isolators: masking transformers of 140M, 243M and 374M parameters, 20 ms of latency, enrolling the caller from the call itself. Short evaluation windows hide two failures that real calls expose: forgetting the caller when another voice talks alone for a while, and damaging a caller who is alone. Long calls with turns, memory beyond the attention window, real headset crosstalk and drifting caller levels address both, but each trades one against the other. WavLM-Large's own weights, made causal and trained with the model, move the trade: M with them (555M parameters) lowers the error on our development sets from 11.44% to 10.55%; a student trained from scratch to imitate WavLM does not, and w2v-BERT 2.0 and Whisper's encoder, pre-trained on far more audio, help less or not at all. A lone caller loses most at the start of a recording: no training call opened with someone already talking. Training on windows cut from longer calls lowers the error on clean development calls from 3.92% to 2.96%; this is our release. Live, the release makes 16.13% word errors on 60 s AMI windows, against 23.66% for VoxLock, the strongest open isolator, and 10.19% on its own AMI windows, against 11.71%; it is level on Krisp's benchmark (5.74% against 5.63%), and a caller who is alone still loses more words than with VoxLock (5.58% against 2.92% on clean test calls). Distilled into 22.1M parameters without WavLM, it runs live on one CPU thread inside a LiveKit agent, at 33% of a core per call in 20 ms frames, with 10.66% error on our development sets (the release 10.49%). We open-source the release and this CPU model, with a LiveKit plugin, at https://huggingface.co/collections/Scicom-intl/voice-isolator.

Trainable Boundary-Keeping Where No Formal Answer Exists: A Controlled Knock-In Study of Reward Training in Evidence-Sufficiency Judgment
在无正式答案存在的情况下实现可训练的边界保持：奖励训练在证据充分性判断中的受控敲入研究
Reasoning-tuned and reward-trained models are often assumed to verify more reliably because they reason longer or receive correctness signals. We test this in evidence-sufficiency judgment: deciding whether available information actually supports a causal claim, a domain with no decidable correctness reward. Using a pre-registered, same-base, controlled knock-in design, we compare a boundary-keeping recipe (SFT then GRPO) with its own baseline, a scrambled-pairing placebo, and a general-purpose reasoning model under an action-pressure protocol with no evaluation invitation. All load-bearing outcomes are rated by two separate model-rating sessions masked to arm labels; automatic judges only trigger. The trained arm raises spontaneous correct refusal from 25% to 100% (40 per arm; Wilson 95% CI lower bound 91.2%, non-overlapping with the baseline interval [14.2%, 40.2%]), while the scrambled placebo collapses (5% spontaneous / 7.5% invited correct; 91.1% false refusal). The effect is boundary-specific rather than blanket refusal: automatic false refusal on 281 well-formed claims is 1.1% (Wilson upper bound 3.09%), and a targeted 18-item arm-(c) recheck (3 flagged plus 15 accepted) yields 0/18 and 1/18 false refusals in two sessions. The dissociation is the main result: final boundary-keeping is trainable without an inference-time verifier, while observed active numeric/calculation checking in the H3 assay remains near zero; SFT saturation makes the GRPO increment not separately identifiable. A pre-registered mechanism adjudication favors reward internalization of final-action status (H2, best-supported, not proven). The scope is a controlled 14B same-family study: we do not claim proof, cross-family generality, or independent human-expert validation; the rating sessions are model sessions, not human reviewers.

通常认为，经过推理调优和奖励训练的模型更具可靠性，因为它们能进行更长时间的推理或接收正确性信号。我们在证据充分性判断任务中检验这一假设：判断现有信息是否真正支持因果主张，这是一个不存在可判定正确性奖励的领域。采用注册过的、同基础的受控敲入设计，我们将一种边界保持方法（SFT后接GRPO）与自身基线、随机配对安慰剂以及通用推理模型进行比较，实验在无评价邀请的动作压力协议下进行。所有关键结果由两轮独立的模型评分会话评定，且对分组标签盲化；自动裁判仅在触发时启用。训练组自发拒绝正确答案的比例从25%提升至100%（每组40例；Wilson 95%置信区间下限91.2%，与基线区间[14.2%, 40.2%]不重叠），而安慰剂组崩溃（自发正确拒绝5%，受邀正确拒绝7.5%；虚假拒绝率达91.1%）。该效应是特定于边界的，而非普遍拒绝：对281个结构良好的主张，自动虚假拒绝率为1.1%（Wilson上限3.09%）；针对18项目标检查（3个标记+15个接受）的再检查结果显示，两轮会话中分别为0/18和1/18的虚假拒绝。主要发现是：无需推理时验证器，最终的边界保持行为是可训练的，而H3检测中观察到的主动数值/计算检查仍接近零；SFT饱和导致GRPO增量无法单独识别。注册机制裁定支持奖励内部化最终动作状态（H2，最佳支持，非证明）。本研究为受控的14B同家族研究，我们不声称证明、跨家族泛化或独立人类专家验证；评分会话为模型评分，非人工评审。

Improving VLMs on Scientific Chart Analysis via Autonomous Evolution
通过自主演化改进VLM在科学图表分析中的表现
Understanding and operating with scientific charts is a standard approach in data analysis, and while humans are good at interpreting such charts, open vision-language models (VLMs) are known to perform poorly when it comes to question answering based on such data types. Motivated by an initial observation that many of their errors are due to inexact answering, we raise the following natural question: how much accuracy can we recover without changing the model at all? In this paper, we study this question by searching over inference programs and the code around a "frozen" version of the model. Using ideas from autonomous evolution (famously used in AlphaEvolve), we first start from a baseline inference program, and in each round we show an LLM judge the code together with a few failures on training questions, and ask for an improving evolutionary move. As usual in autonomous evolution approaches, the candidate programs are kept in a small pool ranked by training accuracy, and the next edit is performed on top-scorers from this pool. We run this approach on three VLMs and four popular benchmarks on scientific charts, and we measure the fraction of descriptive questions whose answer exactly matches the ground truth. The accuracy improves in all experimental settings. On average, it rises from 16.6% with the starting program to 41.3% with the evolved one, and the largest single increase is 55.2 percentage points. As a side benefit, our evolved program is 3.8x faster than the starting program, because short answers are easier to grade and faster to generate. Our results demonstrate that a large part of the observed errors arise due to the inference pipeline, and that optimizing it can improve the "frozen" VLM without the need to retrain it.

理解和操作科学图表是数据分析中的标准方法，尽管人类擅长解读此类图表，但开放的视觉-语言模型（VLMs）在基于此类数据类型的问题回答上表现不佳。受初始观察启发——许多错误源于不精确的回答，我们提出一个自然问题：在不改变模型本身的前提下，我们能恢复多少准确性？本文通过搜索“冻结”模型版本的推理程序及其周围代码来研究此问题。借鉴自主演化思想（如AlphaEvolve中所用），我们从一个基线推理程序出发，每轮让LLM裁判查看代码及若干训练问题的失败案例，并要求其提出改进的演化动作。如同典型的自主演化方法，候选程序保留在一个小池中，按训练准确率排序，下一编辑在该池中的高分者上执行。我们在三个VLMs和四个流行的科学图表基准上运行此方法，测量描述性问题中答案与真实值完全匹配的比例。所有实验设置中准确率均有提升。平均而言，从起始程序的16.6%提升至演化后的41.3%，最大单次提升达55.2个百分点。作为附加收益，我们演化的程序比起始程序快3.8倍，因为简短答案更容易评分且生成更快。我们的结果表明，大部分观察到的错误源于推理流程，优化该流程可在无需重新训练的情况下提升“冻结”VLM的表现。

Reinforcement Learning Done Right for Explicit Confidence Targets
为明确置信度目标正确地进行强化学习
Large language models (LLMs) can produce plausible but incorrect answers when they are uncertain, which can mislead users and undermine model reliability. Training models to abstain with reinforcement learning is a natural approach, but most existing methods use a fixed error penalty and therefore cannot adapt their behavior to different confidence requirements at inference time. We study \emph{explicit confidence targets}, where a user specifies a target \(p\) in the prompt and the model directly chooses whether to answer or abstain, with the goal of achieving an accuracy of at least \(p\) among answered questions. However, learning to respond to different confidence targets with a single model has proven difficult, and prior attempts have failed to distinguish different targets. We show that this failure comes from two problems: the reward signal that distinguishes different values of $p$ is often lost during optimization, while the original error penalty grows without bound as $p$ approaches one. We propose RLEC (\textbf{R}einforcement \textbf{L}earning with \textbf{E}xplicit \textbf{C}onfidence Targets), which preserves the learning signal needed to distinguish confidence targets, introduces a stable reward family that keeps the desired answer condition unchanged, and uses reward scheduling to balance effective learning and training stability. Together, these designs enable the first successful training of a single LLM for explicit confidence target control. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks and model scales show that RLEC largely preserves general capabilities and achieves competitive calibration performance. RLEC also supports fine-grained target control without an external decision system or threshold calibration after training. By making explicit confidence targets part of the trained policy, RLEC opens a new and more direct path toward behavioral calibration.
中文翻译
大型语言模型（LLMs）在不确定时可能生成看似合理但错误的答案，这会误导用户并削弱模型可靠性。使用强化学习训练模型选择回避是一种自然方法，但大多数现有方法采用固定的错误惩罚，因此无法在推理时根据不同的置信度需求调整行为。我们研究了 extit{明确置信度目标}，即用户在提示中指定目标值$p$，模型直接决定是否回答或回避，目标是使回答问题的准确率至少达到$p$。然而，让单一模型适应不同置信度目标一直很困难，先前尝试未能有效区分不同目标。我们发现这种失败源于两个问题：区分不同$p$值的奖励信号在优化过程中常被丢失，而原始错误惩罚随$p$趋近于1时无界增长。我们提出RLEC（ extbf{R}einforcement extbf{L}earning with extbf{E}xplicit extbf{C}onfidence Targets），它保留了区分置信度目标所需的学习除了信号，引入稳定的奖励族以保持期望回答条件不变，并使用奖励调度平衡有效学习与训练稳定性。这些设计共同实现了首个成功训练单一LLM以实现明确置信度目标控制。在多种基准和模型规模上的大量实验表明，RLEC在很大程度上保持了通用能力，并实现了有竞争力的校准性能。RLEC还支持无需外部决策系统或训练后阈值校准的细粒度目标控制。通过将明确置信度目标纳入训练策略，RLEC开辟了一条更直接、更高效的行为校准新路径。

Reason or Recite: Complementary Specialists with an LLM Judge for Traffic Anomaly Reasoning
推理还是复述：基于LLM裁判的交通异常推理双专家框架
Road anomalies such as collisions, violations, and sudden hazards demand more from video understanding than detection: a practical system must verify what happened, describe the scene, and explain the cause. We find these competences pull in opposite directions for vision-language models: closed-form questions reward precise, evidence-grounded reasoning, while open-ended answers are scored by similarity to reference text, where matching the annotation style matters as much as reasoning correctly. We present Reason-or-Recite (RoR), a two-specialist framework for the Traffic Anomaly Reasoning track of the 2026 AI City Challenge. RoR (1) rewrites the official chain-of-thought annotations into a structured, temporally grounded schema and LoRA-tunes a 9B vision-language model on the enhanced traces; (2) fine-tunes a 4-bit-quantized 27B model on answers alone, absorbing the annotation style; and (3) selects between the two candidates per question with a training-free LLM judge. RoR ranks first on the in-domain leaderboard with mean score 0.6788.

Improving Reasoning with Rollout Agreement for Group-Based Policy Optimization
基于回溯一致性的群体策略优化中推理性能的提升
Recent methods for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) use rollout diversity to improve reasoning performance or training efficiency. Despite these gains, the extent to which differences among correct-answer rollouts reflect useful alternative reasoning or unresolved errors remains poorly understood. We investigate this question through a blind paired analysis of a model trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), comparing the highest- and lowest-agreement correct-answer traces for the same problem. Across 126 pairs, low-agreement traces have more spurious reasoning than high-agreement traces (35% vs. 22%), including internal inconsistencies and misuse of problem conditions. Based on these findings, we propose RoAR (Rollout-Agreement Reward), which adds reasoning-level agreement to GRPO's rewards for verified-correct rollouts. RoAR computes this signal from existing on-policy rollout groups, requiring no human-written rationales, additional sampling, or separately trained process evaluator. On five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the 1.5B GRPO-RoAR model reaches 55.5% mean pass@1 under zero-shot evaluation using 7K training examples, exceeding GRPO and GRPO-CARE by 6.0 and 5.5 percentage points. A separate blind audit of 100 problems answered correctly by all four 1.5B models finds spurious rates of 18% for GRPO-RoAR, 32% for GRPO, 27% for GRPO-CARE, and 37% for DRA-GRPO. Our findings identify reasoning validity as an important consideration when using rollout differences to guide learning. Our code is available at https://github.com/ldi-kyunghee/RoAR.

近期采用可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）方法利用回溯多样性来提升推理表现或训练效率。尽管取得进展，但正确回溯之间的差异究竟反映的是有用的替代推理路径，还是未解决的错误仍不清楚。我们通过盲法成对分析一个使用群体相对策略优化（GRPO）训练的模型，比较同一问题中高一致性和低一致性的正确回溯轨迹。在126组对比中，低一致性轨迹的虚假推理比例更高（35% vs. 22%），包括内部不一致和误用问题条件。基于此发现，我们提出RoAR（回溯一致性奖励），在GRPO的可验证正确回溯奖励中加入推理层面的一致性信号。RoAR从现有的在线回溯组中计算该信号，无需人工编写推理过程、额外采样或独立训练的过程评估器。在五个数学推理基准测试中，1.5B规模的GRPO-RoAR模型在零样本评估下使用7K训练样本达到55.5%的mean pass@1，优于GRPO和GRPO-CARE 6.0和5.5个百分点。对四个1.5B模型均正确回答的100个问题的独立盲审显示，虚假推理率分别为：GRPO-RoAR为18%，GRPO为32%，GRPO-CARE为27%，DRA-GRPO为37%。我们的研究强调，在利用回溯差异指导学习时，推理有效性是一个重要考量因素。代码已公开于https://github.com/ldi-kyunghee/RoAR。

Correlation-Aware Exploration for Long-Trace Reasoning
面向长推理轨迹的关联感知探索
Reasoning models trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) now produce chains of thought thousands of tokens long, and recent studies reveal that such training is prone to policy collapse. Entropy regularization is the standard remedy, but it works by pushing probability mass away from the few tokens that carry it and toward the vast low-probability tail of the vocabulary, and it applies this force once for every token of the reasoning trace. This puts the bonus in direct conflict with the entropy decay that convergence requires, and makes its coefficient difficult to set in the long-trace regime. To resolve this tension, we propose Info-GRPO, an information-theoretic framework that cultivates correlation between the policy and a latent prior. Rather than raising entropy everywhere, Info-GRPO builds on the mutual information between a latent variable and the trajectory it induces: augmenting prompts with latent seeds during training lets the model explore diverse policies correlated with the prior, while the seed-conditioned entropy is guided toward convergence. Diversity is therefore carried across whole reasoning traces rather than by per-token randomness, and exploration no longer fights entropy reduction. Experiments show that Info-GRPO outperforms vanilla GRPO and entropy-regularized GRPO across diverse reasoning benchmarks. On AIME24, it improves $Avg@8$ over GRPO by 3.75%, 1.66%, 4.16%, and 4.17% on four backbones, and it reaches the same majority-vote accuracy with $8\times$ fewer samples. Code and models will be publicly released.

ThinkBit: Search Codewords, Recalibrate Scales, Select by Reasoning
ThinkBit：搜索码字、重新校准尺度、基于推理的选择
Reasoning language models generate thousands of tokens per answer, and generation speed is limited by memory bandwidth, so storing weights in two bits instead of bfloat16 can potentially make inference 8$\times$ cheaper. Two-bit methods are usually judged by perplexity and multiple-choice question-answering accuracy, both of which say little about whether a model can still reason through more difficult problems. We present ThinkBit, a strictly scalar two-bit framework built to preserve reasoning, in which every weight is an integer codeword times a bfloat16 scale shared by a group of weights. We first use a sensitivity metric to assign each layer a ternary, 2-bit, or 3-bit tier to allocate bitwidths optimally among layers. This is followed by a layerwise Gumbel-softmax-based scalar quantization algorithm that searches for optimal codewords block by block. Since a layerwise scheme does not capture how quantized layers interact with each other, we recalibrate scales, with the codewords frozen, using a knowledge-distillation-based loss against the teacher model. We then perform a short quantization-aware training (QAT) stage that lets the model mimic the base model's distribution by reassigning codewords. Finally, a paired reasoning test on training problems selects the final checkpoint between the recalibration stage and the QAT stage. On Qwen3-1.7B at matched size, our recalibrated checkpoint scores 46.7 on MATH-500 against 30.0 for EfficientQAT trained on the same data, and 73.0 after QAT on reasoning traces; at 0.52 GB it is smaller than every published 2-bit GGUF of the model yet more accurate on MATH-500. We show that this framework scales and up to 14B, a 3.74 GB model scores 94.8 on MATH-500, against 97.5 for the 29.5 GB bfloat16 model.
中文翻译
推理型语言模型每答案生成数千token，推理速度受限于内存带宽，因此将权重存储为2比特而非bfloat16可能使推理成本降低8倍。然而，2比特方法通常以困惑度和多选题问答准确率为评价标准，这些指标无法反映模型是否仍能处理更复杂的问题。我们提出ThinkBit，一种严格标量化的2比特框架，旨在保留推理能力，其中每个权重为整数码字乘以一组权重共享的bfloat16尺度。我们首先使用敏感性度量为每一层分配三值、2比特或3比特层级，以最优分配各层比特宽度。随后采用基于Gumbel-softmax的分层标量量化算法，逐块搜索最优码字。由于分层方案无法捕捉量化层间的相互影响，我们冻结码字后，通过知识蒸馏损失对尺度进行重新校准。接着执行简短的量化感知训练（QAT）阶段，让模型通过重新分配码字模仿基础模型的分布。最后，通过对训练问题进行配对推理测试，在重新校准阶段和QAT阶段之间选择最终检查点。在与Qwen3-1.7B同尺寸下，我们的重新校准检查点在MATH-500上得分为46.7，而EfficientQAT在同一数据上训练的结果仅为30.0，经QAT后推理轨迹得分达73.0；在0.52 GB大小下，小于所有已发布的该模型2比特GGUF版本，且在MATH-500上更准确。我们还证明该框架可扩展至14B规模，3.74 GB模型在MATH-500上得分为94.8，接近29.5 GB bfloat16模型的97.5分。

Priority-Preserving Advantage Aggregation for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization
优先级保持的优势聚合用于多奖励策略优化
LLM post-training often optimizes multiple objectives with unequal priorities, such as correctness and reasoning efficiency. However, the widely used additive reward aggregation in RL can violate these priorities: when primary and auxiliary advantages conflict, a sufficiently large auxiliary signal can overturn the preference induced by the primary objective. We term this problem \emph{advantage priority inversion}. Although reward-level gating can protect priority more directly, it still removes potentially useful auxiliary distinctions among rollout samples that fail the primary condition. To address this trade-off, we propose Primary Advantage Policy Optimization (\textbf{PAPO}), a priority-aware advantage aggregation method that asymmetrically combines a primary and an auxiliary advantage. PAPO retains auxiliary supervision when the objectives agree and smoothly attenuates conflicting auxiliary signals, preserving the primary sign during fusion for \emph{primary-consistent ordering}. This rule applies to sequence-level advantages in GRPO and token-level advantages in actor--critic PPO. Experiments on multiple domains and models show that PAPO consistently achieves the best primary objective while maintaining best or competitive auxiliary-objective performance across both GRPO- and PPO-based optimization. \href{https://xiangchi-yuan.github.io/papo-project/}{Code is available}.
中文翻译
大语言模型的后训练通常需要优化多个具有不同优先级的目标，例如正确性和推理效率。然而，强化学习中广泛使用的加性奖励聚合方法可能违背这些优先级：当主要目标与辅助目标的优势冲突时，足够大的辅助信号可能会逆转由主要目标引发的偏好。我们称此问题为“优势优先级反转”。尽管在奖励层面进行门控可以更直接地保护优先级，但它仍会移除那些未能满足主要条件的回溯样本中潜在有用的辅助区分信息。为解决这一权衡，我们提出了一种优先级感知的优势聚合方法——主优势策略优化（PAPO），该方法不对称地结合主优势和辅助优势。PAPO 在目标一致时保留辅助监督，并平滑衰减冲突的辅助信号，在融合过程中保持主优势符号不变，实现‘主一致性排序’。该规则适用于GRPO中的序列级优势和PPO中的词元级优势。在多个领域和模型上的实验表明，PAPO在持续取得最佳主目标表现的同时，也保持了最优或具有竞争力的辅助目标性能，适用于基于GRPO和PPO的优化。代码已公开。

Mechanistic Insights into LoRA: Layer Sparsity for Adaptive Fine-Tuning via Path Patching
LoRA的机制洞察：通过路径修补实现自适应微调的层稀疏性
Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as the dominant paradigm for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. Standard all-layer LoRA applies adaptation throughout the transformer, despite heterogeneous contributions from its components. In this work, we conduct a systematic mechanistic interpretability analysis to understand how LoRA affects model internals. We observe that LoRA's adaptation effect is highly non-uniform, with significant component-wise and layer-wise sparsity. Most critically, we find that important layers are highly task-dependent, with limited overlap across tasks. Motivated by these insights, we propose Adaptive-LoRA, a calibration-driven method that automatically identifies task-specific layers via frozen-base zero-ablation, enabling efficient layer selection without exhaustive search. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-1.5B across 11 diverse reasoning tasks demonstrate that Adaptive-LoRA outperforms full-layer LoRA while using only 30% of layers, achieving a $3.5\times$ reduction in adapter parameters. This work bridges mechanistic interpretability and practical efficiency, providing both fundamental insights and a principled approach for adaptive fine-tuning.

Knowing When the Evidence Is Enough: Requirement-Directed Search with Horn-Closure Certificates
何时证据已足够：基于Horn闭包证书的需求导向搜索
After each Web search, a search-augmented model must decide whether its evidence suffices: answer, search again, or abstain. Prevailing systems leave this to holistic model judgement, which can accept a context naming every entity yet lacking one required fact. We instead make sufficiency structural: a per-query requirement hypergraph states which facts jointly yield another fact. This raises two challenges: deriving requirements from the question alone, and linking each requirement to passages about the right entity. Certify therefore decomposes the question, searches per requirement, and accepts links only after entity checks. Horn closure over the links yields a certificate, the minimal sufficient passages and their derivation, or an abstention naming open requirements. Given correct retrieval, requirements and links, the decision is sound, and complete up to the entity check. Pooled over three corpora with unanswerable twins, Certify decides significantly more accurately than search agents, graph retrieval and sufficiency judges in default configurations. On the same evidence, it matches a proprietary model's sufficiency label without an additional model call. Over 21M Wikipedia passages, entity checks add 4 to 13 points of decision accuracy where gold evidence exists. Finally, answers from its certificate are 80% correct, against 57% from all retrieved passages.
中文翻译
每次网络搜索后，搜索增强型模型必须判断其证据是否充分：回答、再次搜索或放弃。现有系统将此决策交由整体模型判断，可能导致接受一个列出所有实体但缺少必要事实的上下文。我们则将充分性结构化：每个查询的需求超图明确指出哪些事实联合可推导出另一事实。这带来两个挑战：仅从问题中推导需求，以及将每个需求与涉及正确实体的段落关联。Certify因此分解问题，按需求分别搜索，并在完成实体验证后才接受链接。对链接进行Horn闭包运算生成证书，即最小充分段落及其推导过程，或因未闭合需求而放弃。在正确检索、需求和链接的前提下，该决策是可靠的，且在实体检查范围内是完备的。在三个包含无法回答孪生样本的语料库上，Certify在默认配置下比搜索代理、图检索和充分性判断器显著更准确。在相同证据下，它无需额外模型调用即可匹配专有模型的充分性标签。在超过2100万维基百科段落上，实体验证使有真实证据情况下的决策准确率提升4至13个百分点。最终，其证书生成的答案正确率为80%，远高于从所有检索段落中获得的57%。

Agent Memory as Recommendation: Recommender-System Design for Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents
智能体记忆即推荐：面向LLM智能体长期记忆的推荐系统设计
Large language model (LLM) agents that serve users across many sessions must choose, for every request, the few stored memories that enter a limited context window. This choice largely decides whether the agent answers correctly, and it runs on every request at Web scale. This selection faces three challenges: a large and growing store, a per-request cost budget, and multi-session questions that need all of their evidence. Many memory systems build notes or graphs with hundreds to thousands of LLM calls per history, and each is designed on its own, so it is unclear which component yields the accuracy. These challenges mirror the properties of recommendation, so we formalize agent memory as budgeted slate recommendation, with the request as the user, stored memories as items and the context window as a slate. The formalization places memory systems in one design space of recommender cascades and factorizes accuracy into the completeness that each stage controls. Guided by it, we propose AgentMemRec, which adapts candidate generation, learning to rank and slate construction from recommender systems and selects memories without any LLM call. On multi-session questions of LongMemEval, AgentMemRec outperforms memory and context-selection methods, including A-Mem, HippoRAG 2, DynamicRAG and T-Mem, by 10 to 31 points of accuracy. It matches an LLM reranker that makes 64 calls per query at 3.2 times lower serving cost, and on LoCoMo it outperforms Mem0 and Zep without any LLM call at write time. The factorization attributes the gains to slates that more often hold all of the evidence, so recommender-system design offers an effective and efficient foundation for the long-term memory of LLM agents.
中文翻译
服务于多会话用户的大型语言模型（LLM）智能体必须为每次请求选择少数存储的记忆进入有限的上下文窗口。这一选择很大程度决定了智能体能否正确回答问题，且需在Web规模上每请求执行一次。该选择面临三大挑战：庞大的不断增长的记忆库、每次请求的成本预算，以及需要整合全部证据的跨会话问题。许多记忆系统构建笔记或图谱，每历史记录需数百至数千次LLM调用，且各自独立设计，因此难以确定哪个组件带来准确性提升。这些挑战与推荐系统特性高度相似，因此我们将智能体记忆形式化为带预算的板面推荐问题：请求为用户，存储记忆为物品，上下文窗口为板面。该形式化将记忆系统置于推荐级联的设计空间中，并将准确性分解为各阶段所控制的完整性。基于此，我们提出AgentMemRec，借鉴推荐系统的候选生成、学习排序和板面构建方法，无需任何LLM调用即可选择记忆。在LongMemEval的跨会话问题上，AgentMemRec在准确率上优于记忆选择和上下文选择方法（包括A-Mem、HippoRAG 2、DynamicRAG和T-Mem），提升10至31个百分点。其性能相当于每查询调用64次LLM的重排序器，但服务成本仅为后者的1/3.2；在LoCoMo数据集上，其性能超越Mem0和Zep，且在写入时无需任何LLM调用。因子化分析表明，性能提升源于板面更常包含全部证据，因此推荐系统设计为LLM智能体的长期记忆提供了有效且高效的基石。

Effective tutoring requires determining not only what information to provide, but also which form of assistance to deliver. A tutor may address the same student error using various pedagogical strategies, adapting its approach as the interaction progresses. We introduce Comparative Pedagogical Supervision (CPS), a training framework to learn to select the optimal strategy and feedback for student learning. We evaluate CPS on math and science reasoning datasets. After five tutoring turns, CPS outperforms the strongest fixed-strategy baselines. The learned tutor transfers across datasets, and its strategy selection can also inform a separate API-based tutor.

How do later loops in a pretrained looped language model repair two-hop retrieval? We study Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B by transplanting attention queries between loops at the same layer, head and final prompt position. On synthetic in-context questions, injecting the layer-indexed collection of loop-3 queries throughout loop 1 rescues 90% and 97% of questions answered incorrectly at loop 1 and correctly at loop 3, versus 24% and 21% for shuffled donors. The rescue also holds under greedy generation in Ouro-2.6B; in Ouro-1.4B it is limited to four-candidate ranking. Crossed donor-recipient swaps favor retrieval through the donor's bridge entity over copying its answer, although a substantial positional component remains in Ouro-2.6B. Late keys and values rescue far fewer targets. Freezing queries at their loop-1 values also damages two-hop accuracy more than a matched question that supplies the bridge. On natural questions, rescue is smaller and replicates only in Ouro-2.6B, and crossed swaps do not establish bridge redirection. These results identify a transferable collection of late-loop queries that supports bridge-conditioned retrieval on synthetic scenes; they do not locate where the bridge is computed or establish a single-vector handoff.

Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine
波即一切：基于全连接量子玻尔兹曼机的量子语言模型
This work proposes a self-attention mechanism based on the fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine (FC-QBM), and further constructs a fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine language model (FC-QBM-LM) using the mechanism as the core engine. By performing unitary evolution on semantic quantum states, the mechanism implicitly implements positional encoding and self-attention computation, eliminating the need to decompose continuous semantic streams into discrete matrices for explicit matrix multiplication, with the measurement results naturally satisfying the normalization condition. Specifically, this work rigorously derives the computational principle of the self-attention mechanism based on FC-QBM, and demonstrates that this mechanism is mathematically equivalent to the classical self-attention mechanism. The mathematical principles governing the training and generation of FC-QBM-LM are thoroughly derived, and the two corresponding algorithms are subsequently developed. An 8-qubit FC-QBM-LM is finally constructed and trained on the corpus of Tang poetry. Under the 8-qubit setting, the quantum layer implements the entire positional encoding and self-attention computation pipeline with only 44 parameters. In the noiseless scenario, the model exhibits favorable convergence. Furthermore, the quantum circuit proposed in this work, which terminates with Y-axis rotation gates, achieves better convergence than the counterpart terminating with X-axis rotation gates. Under the small-sample regime and across eight distinct noise intensity levels, the model demonstrates strong noise robustness, retaining over 99% of its noiseless convergence performance. Experiments on five-character quatrain generation reveal that the model preliminarily exhibits three core capabilities: associative and divergent thinking, content generation across imagery and human-aligned word ordering.

What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents
我应该选择多大的努力程度？关于大语言模型智能体推理努力的经济学分析
Generative models increasingly expose a reasoning effort setting that lets users scale inference-time compute, trading higher cost for potentially improved performance. Users must choose an effort level before knowing whether extra reasoning will help, and even a successful run does not reveal whether the effort purchased was necessary. Reasoning effort is therefore a credence good: buyers observe the outcome but cannot assess the marginal value of the computation they paid for. In this work, we measure the counterfactual effect of effort levels on both proprietary and open-weight models on four benchmarks, spanning single-call reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks. Effort, it turns out, does not consistently preserve tasks that lower effort solves, can overspend, and can change trajectory behavior. First, we find that although higher effort can raise accuracy in aggregate, it frequently fails on tasks that lower effort solved. Second, on the subset of easy tasks that every effort level solves, higher effort is generally more costly, with the highest effort level costing up to 42x as much as the lowest. Lastly, effort changes not only how many tokens are used, but also how agents solve tasks: at higher effort, agents verify their own work more heavily and more often search for solutions than work through problems directly, both of which lengthen trajectories without necessarily altering the outcome. These findings show that naively choosing the highest level is not only cost-inefficient but also offers no guarantee of the best instance-level performance. A simple alternative, starting at the lowest effort and escalating only after a verified failure, matches or improves on fixed top effort across all models and benchmarks at lower cost for most proprietary models.

Scientific literature in materials physics is growing faster than researchers can manually inspect it, yet most retrieval tools rely on keyword matching or generic question answering that ignores domain-specific structure in PDF files. This paper presents an end-to-end pipeline that transforms arXiv superconductivity publications into a searchable corpus with structured metadata and retrieval-augmented question answering. The system combines thematic corpus construction, domain-aware extraction of materials and superconducting transition temperatures, and hybrid retrieval that merges dense chunk embeddings with structured publication fields. We test whether normalized domain attributes improve evidence retrieval and answer groundedness relative to lexical-only and dense text-only methods. Extraction is evaluated on a manually verified gold set of 59 superconducting materials, 46 of which have confirmed experimental critical temperatures. On the 33-material primary positive subset, domain-aware pair accuracy reaches 45.5% versus 9.1% for a regex baseline. Retrieval and generation are compared under a fixed language model (qwen2.5:7b-instruct) on a 100-question benchmark, varying only the retrieval mechanism: BM25, dense, hybrid, and hybrid with domain metadata. BM25 gives the highest source recall (Recall@5 of 47%), and adding extracted metadata to hybrid retrieval does not improve it (39% versus 41%), which we attribute to noise in the extracted fields; the main bottleneck is locating the supporting span inside a correctly retrieved paper. As a materials-informatics application, literature-derived temperatures are matched to an independent theoretical reference set: 200 materials appear in both sources, and 20 have a median experimental critical temperature above the theoretical value.

AndroidFlux: Evaluating and Reward Modeling Failure Recovery Capabilities in Mobile Use Multimodal Agents

Mobile-use multimodal agents are typically evaluated by task success from a clean initial state, which does not isolate their ability to recover from intermediate errors. Because mobile environments change dynamically, a general mobile-use agent must complete tasks robustly even from unexpected states and in unseen environments. This requires knowing when and where an agent makes errors, and whether it can recover from errors and subsequent states. To evaluate this capability, we introduce AndroidFlux, a failure-recovery benchmark built on AndroidWorld. AndroidFlux restores recorded trajectories to controlled checkpoints before, at, and after the first recoverable error, so that different agents continue from the same device state and history. On these checkpoints, a complementary reward-modeling benchmark evaluates recovery-action preferences using downstream rollout outcomes. We further release an offline reinforcement learning (RL) dataset that improves both error recovery and overall task success. Our evaluations show that recovery performance only partially correlates with clean-start success, and that explicit reasoning helps only models trained with GUI-domain specific RL.

Whether or Where? Tail Calibration Signals Finite-Budget Reward Hacking in Best-of-N Selection

Best-of-N (BoN) inference returns the candidate with the highest proxy reward, so a larger $N$ tests the proxy's extreme tail more than its average ranking quality. We show that the exact BoN value is a Beta-weighted integral of conditional true reward over within-prompt score quantiles. It follows that BoN depends on scores only through their ranks. It also follows that BoN can decline only if the calibration curve in the tail turns downward, and the budget where the decline appears depends on where that turn lies. Under a bounded additive model, the error tail sets the limit: Gaussian errors keep improving, Laplace errors reach a plateau, and heavy-tailed errors return to the prior mean. When error variance is largest at low true reward, even Gaussian noise can push BoN below random selection. Synthetic phase maps agree with this taxonomy. On real candidate pools spanning several verifiable domains, base policies, and learned reward models, tail failures are rare and all occur in code generation. A held-out tail calibration statistic reliably predicts where a cross-fitted budget cap helps. It does about as well as rank accuracy, and the cap is competitive with a Soft-BoN baseline. Tail calibration therefore does not replace ranking metrics. It is an audit that is unchanged by any monotone rescaling of the reward scores and shows which budgets are at risk.

最佳N（BoN）推理返回代理奖励最高的候选者，因此更大的N值会更深入测试代理奖励的极端尾部，而非其平均排名质量。我们证明，精确的BoN值是条件真实奖励在提示内得分分位数上的Beta加权积分。由此可知，BoN仅依赖于得分的排名，而不依赖于具体数值。同时，BoN下降仅当尾部校准曲线向下弯曲时才会发生，且下降出现的预算取决于该弯曲的位置。在受限加法模型下，误差尾部设定了上限：高斯误差持续改善，拉普拉斯误差达到平台期，重尾误差则回归先验均值。当误差方差在低真实奖励处最大时，即使高斯噪声也可能使BoN低于随机选择。合成相图与该分类一致。在涵盖多个可验证领域、基础策略和学习奖励模型的真实候选池中，尾部失败罕见，且全部出现在代码生成任务中。保留的尾部校准统计量能可靠预测交叉拟合预算上限的作用位置。其表现与排名准确率相当，且该上限与Soft-BoN基线具有竞争力。因此，尾部校准并未取代排名指标，而是一种不受任何单调重缩放影响的审计手段，可揭示哪些预算处于风险之中。

Birth, Death and Diff: Insertion-Based Sequence Generation with Corrections

Insertion-based masked diffusion models enable flexible-length, parallel generation by interleaving mask insertion with token unmasking. However, because their generation decisions are irreversible, aggressive parallel decoding can introduce errors that subsequent steps cannot correct, necessitating conservative decoding with more forward passes (NFEs). Moreover, they exhibit higher entropy than standard MDMs because they marginalize over multiple alignments during training and therefore require even more conservative decoding in the absence of a correction mechanism. To address this limitation, we introduce $δ$MDM, which makes intermediate generations revisable by equipping an insertion-based model with substitution and deletion operations. During training, we expose the model to errors caused by aggressive unmasking and insertion, teaching it to correct its own mistakes. At inference time, we interleave insertion and unmasking with correction steps that can revise previously unmasked tokens and remove unnecessary masks. This mechanism makes aggressive decoding practical, improving both generation speed and quality. $δ$MDM Pareto-dominates FlexMDM, a vanilla insertion-based MDM, on the speed--quality trade-off. On high-diversity unconditional text generation on OpenWebText, it halves the generative perplexity relative to FlexMDM at the highest inference budget. It also achieves lower generative perplexity at all inference budgets compared to MDM trained from scratch with variable-length padded sequences. On low-diversity conditional text generation on TinyGSM, it matches FlexMDM accuracy with half as many NFEs.

Entropic Control for Homeostatic Optimization: Pre-empting Catastrophic Forgetting via Dynamic Feedback

Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) of LLMs suffers from catastrophic forgetting, and prevailing mitigation strategies struggle to reconcile the plasticity-stability dilemma. To address this, we propose Entropic Control for Homeostatic Optimization (ECHO), a closed-loop control framework. By decomposing the KL divergence, we identify output entropy as a dominant observable component of KL variation. This enables us to leverage entropy as a computationally efficient online proxy to monitor forgetting risks in real-time, bypassing expensive reference-model inference. Consequently, ECHO employs an elastic controller that dynamically modulates the gradient weight of replay data via a proportional control law, using deviations from the pre-trained entropic equilibrium as an error signal. Empirical evaluations across 0.6B to 9B parameter architectures demonstrate that ECHO lies on, and in several comparisons extends, the observed plasticity-stability frontier and maintains high operational robustness against varying data mixing ratios.

Tool-using language model agents are usually evaluated by whether they finish the user's task. That metric misses a common failure: an agent can complete the requested work while also taking an unauthorized side-effecting action, such as writing to the wrong object, expanding the scope of the request, or contacting an unintended recipient. We call this failure mode collateral damage (CD). We introduce SABench (Side-effect-Aware Benchmark), a benchmark of 201 email, calendar, and ticket tasks. Each task crosses one of four state structures (independent, dependent, externally reachable, cross-tool) with one of four trap families (ambiguity, mis-targeting, cascade harm, overreach), and each task has a deterministic trace-based oracle for both goal satisfaction and authorization compliance. Across 2,211 model-task pairs from 11 frontier LLMs spanning major commercial and open model families, 15.2% of all runs incur CD, with risk concentrated in ambiguity tasks (38.8% violation rate) while non-ambiguous traps average 8.4% CD. Among goal-satisfied runs, 12.8% still produce unauthorized writes. Cross-tool and dependent states have about twice the CD rate of independent states. CD rates vary by 4.7x across models at comparable goal rates, which suggests that task success alone is a poor proxy for safe tool use. The SABench task corpus is released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Phaedrus/sabench; the traces, oracle, code, and analysis pipeline are released at https://github.com/hjj194/sabench-artifact.

While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) excel at zero-shot reasoning, their spatial capabilities are primarily evaluated through static, passive observation. In complex, human-centric scenes, occlusion often hides crucial geometric evidence, and passive benchmarks force models to guess rather than recognize their own visual uncertainty. To bridge this gap, we introduce SATE-Bench, a novel interactive benchmark comprising 316 real-world scenes and 2,525 multi-turn QA pairs to evaluate visual self-awareness and active exocentric view-exploration. It combines a Passive multi-view control with an Active exploration setting, where models start from a severely occluded view and must iteratively query adjacent viewpoints until they gather enough evidence to fully ``sate'' the question, scored by a step-penalized efficiency reward. Evaluating state-of-the-art MLLMs reveals that they terminate exploration prematurely while reporting high confidence, and struggle with fine-grained 3D geometric tasks; matched-view controls further attribute the Active--Passive gap primarily to insufficient evidence acquisition. Moreover, fine-tuning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) shows that rewarding view-seeking increases active exploration but lowers overall accuracy, as models over-explore and fail to fuse expanding multi-view contexts across turns. These findings indicate that scaling passive multi-view perception does not intrinsically yield active spatial reasoning, highlighting the need for models that know where to look, how to integrate what they see, and when to stop. Code and data are available at https://gtc-gh.github.io/SATE-Bench/

尽管多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在零样本推理方面表现出色，但其空间能力主要通过静态、被动观察进行评估。在复杂的人类中心场景中，遮挡常常隐藏了关键的几何证据，而被动基准测试迫使模型猜测而非识别自身的视觉不确定性。为弥合这一差距，我们提出了SATE-Bench，一个包含316个真实世界场景和2,525个多轮问答对的新型交互式基准，用于评估视觉自我意识和主动外部视角探索。该基准结合了被动多视角控制与主动探索设置，模型从严重遮挡的视角出发，必须迭代查询相邻视点，直到收集足够证据完全‘满足’问题，评分基于步数惩罚的效率奖励。评估最先进MLLMs发现，它们在报告高置信度的同时过早终止探索，并在细粒度3D几何任务上表现不佳；匹配视角控制进一步表明，主动-被动差距主要源于证据获取不足。此外，使用组相对策略优化（GRPO）微调显示，奖励视点搜索虽增加了主动探索，但降低了整体准确率，因为模型过度探索且无法在多轮中融合扩展的多视角上下文。这些发现表明，单纯扩大被动多视角感知并不能内在产生主动空间推理，凸显了模型需要知道该看哪里、如何整合所见内容以及何时停止的重要性。代码和数据可在https://gtc-gh.github.io/SATE-Bench/获取。

Self-Evolution Reasoner: Continuous Optimization via Policy-Intrinsic Exploration and Exploitation

Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) enables large language models (LLMs) to continuously self-improve their reasoning capabilities. Compared to RLVR's scalar rewards, recent self-supervised on-policy distillation methods leverage denser supervision signals. However, both paradigms suffer from exploration bottlenecks, struggling to escape local optima when the policy fails to sample valid solutions. Relying on external demonstrations can bypass this issue; however, the off-policy nature hinders genuine self-improvement and the mismatched-distribution reasoning can not be fully exploited. In this work, we propose Self-Evolution Policy Optimization (SEPO), a framework that drives continuous reasoning capability evolution via guided exploration and in-distribution exploitation. Specifically, SEPO utilizes labels to elicit correct reasoning from the policy, unlocking the exploration potential. By treating current policy conditioned on this in-distribution reasoning as a self-teacher, SEPO distills the newly discovered solution back into the policy. Through this iterative cycle of policy-intrinsic exploration and exploitation, SEPO achieves robust and continuous capability evolution. Across scientific, tool-use, and complex logical reasoning domains, SEPO consistently achieves the best performance under identical training time or steps, demonstrating superior efficiency and convergence ceilings. Notably, SEPO maintains stable improvements even in scenarios where baselines severely underperform or fail entirely, such as on complex tasks or with small-scale models. Our code is available at https://github.com/Eric8932/SEPO.

Coding agents are given embedding search and code-graph tools on the premise that a repository's structure is something the model lacks and the tool supplies. First, we ablate a localization agent's tool set (grep only; +embedding search; +graph tools; all) on a depth-balanced 160-task split and on all 500 tasks for ten models (six Qwen3 sizes from 0.6B to 32B with five decodings each, an FP8 control, three Gemma 4 sizes; 79k episodes). Structured tools double grep-only accuracy for Qwen3-8B and Gemma 4 E4B; their gain peaks at 17-21 points at 1.7-4B and falls to 4-5 points at 32B (odds ratio 0.77-0.82 per doubling of parameters). From 8B up, about half of that gain is the form of the submission rather than finding the target; the fall from 14B to 32B is a fall in tool uptake at equal grep-only accuracy; and the same 4B size gains or does not gain from a tool depending on the checkpoint. Each extra hop multiplies the odds of correct localization by 0.50-0.67 at every size, and no tool set flattens that gradient: traces show the graph tools' gain is name lookup at hop 0 and one expansion at hop 1, and agents chain expansions in only 12-14% of episodes. A fixed repair model resolves 6-13 of 160 tasks from these localizations (oracle 26). Second, linear probes find direct call edges decodable under a within-anchor, degree-stratified protocol (AUC 0.74; 0.61-0.66 inside agent conversations), but below a lexical baseline (0.99), with two-hop edges at 0.57. Small agents carry a one-hop, largely lexical picture of their repository, in weights and in use. We release the agent, probes, logs and traces.

Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents

Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience. We introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark developed by 50+ domain experts to measure experience-driven improvement in realistic professional workflows. CLE comprises 120 human-authored tasks, each organised as a five-level ladder, yielding 600 levels spanning 89 professional roles across 12 occupational domains. Agents must pass each level to unlock the next, with later levels building on experience accumulated during earlier assignments. An evaluation agent assesses each submission against human-authored rubrics. We compare a single-submission setting with one that provides diagnostic feedback after failure and allows one revision. Across 17 harness-model configurations using frontier LLMs, feedback and revision yield a median completion gain of 5.3 percentage points. Yet the best-performing system clears only 47.7% of levels and completes all five levels in just 23.3% of tasks, highlighting the difficulty of sustained learning from experience for existing frontier LLMs. As such, the dataset can also be used to post-train LLMs to strengthen their continual learning capabilities.
